1	# Statement ledger
     2	
     3	This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
     4	Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
     5	to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels refer to the manuscript
     6	revision 669ccc9 and are written exactly as in its LaTeX source (for
     7	example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was first written and
     8	reviewed at the earlier revision cf979d6. Revision 669ccc9 changed only
     9	prose, titles and figures: every cited label exists in both, and the
    10	mathematical expressions of each cited statement and its proof are the
    11	same in both up to whitespace and braces (script check recorded in
    12	`provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).
    13	
    14	## Scope
    15	
    16	- The "What it states" column is a faithful paraphrase, sometimes
    17	  shortened. The exact statement is the Lean type in
    18	  `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean`; `Audit/<module>/` prints the
    19	  elaborated types.
    20	- The rows cover every public theorem (82) and the 6 definitions whose
    21	  values are stated as facts. The other 37 public definitions (for example
    22	  `kappa`, `delta`, `gauge`, `counts`) only name quantities used in those
    23	  statements and have no rows of their own; read their bodies in the Lean
    24	  source or in `Audit/`.
    25	- The package checks finite, algebraic and scalar steps only: exact
    26	  identities, polynomial and rational certificates, real-power bookkeeping,
    27	  parameter ranges, and a few finite-dimensional inner-product and
    28	  finite-word facts.
    29	- The SPDE itself, stochastic integrals, Gaussian measures, Fourier and
    30	  spectral analysis, operator theory and all limits in time or in a
    31	  regularization are outside Lean. Where a Lean statement needs an analytic
    32	  fact about the model, that fact enters as an explicit hypothesis of the
    33	  theorem (a "supplied hypothesis" below). Lean checks the deduction from
    34	  those hypotheses, not the hypotheses themselves.
    35	- A successful `lake build` is not a verification receipt for the
    36	  manuscript. It shows that the stated Lean theorems are proved from their
    37	  hypotheses; whether a statement matches the manuscript step it is listed
    38	  against is a separate, human judgment recorded in this ledger.
    39	- Three further modules developed alongside these (normalized Gaussian
    40	  coordinates, vector Gaussian projection, and colored vector words) are
    41	  withheld from this package because they depend on a library that is not
    42	  yet public.
    43	- "no direct label" means the declaration checks a computation from the
    44	  development of the manuscript that does not appear as, or inside, a
    45	  labeled statement of the revision cited above. Such rows make no claim
    46	  about the manuscript.
    47	
    48	All declarations live in the namespace `StratonovichHAMAudit.<Module>`; the
    49	file is `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean`. The four `PositiveGram`
    50	declarations have status `internal` in `claims.yaml`; all others are
    51	`reusable`.

   135	## DimensionalMatrix
   136	
   137	Defines the backward, coupling and forward 2x2 phase matrices of a single
   138	interaction and computes their product with all four entries retained, in
   139	unweighted coordinates. At fixed frequencies `r`, `rho` the matrices are
   140	the factors of `S(-t) B(b) S(t)` in `E:variance-physical-adjoint` of
   141	`P:actual-wave-form` (`backward` = `S(-t)`, `coupling` = the force
   142	`B(b)(u, v) = (0, b u)`, `forward` = `S(t)`, with `cp = cos(rt)`,
   143	`sp/p = sin(rt)/r` and the coefficient `H` in place of `b`), and
   144	`full_interaction` is that unweighted product. It is not yet the normalized
   145	kernel `E:variance-normalized-kernel`: there `b_r = <r> sin(rt)/r`
   146	(`L:masked-continuous-wave`), and passing to it needs the Bessel-weighted
   147	change of coordinates on the phase space `E` together with the weight
   148	`1/sqrt(<xi><eta>)`. That conversion, the Fourier interpretation and the
   149	zero-frequency case (where the manuscript uses the continuous sine quotient)
   150	are outside Lean. The free matrix also appears in the proof of
   151	`L:complex-phase` and, in balanced coordinates, as `W_t` in
   152	`L:symplectic-free`, which also defines the force `B(b)`.

1	# Statement ledger
     2	
     3	This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
     4	Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
     5	to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels refer to the manuscript
     6	revision 669ccc9 and are written exactly as in its LaTeX source (for
     7	example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was first written and
     8	reviewed at the earlier revision cf979d6. Revision 669ccc9 changed only
     9	prose, titles and figures: every cited label exists in both, and the
    10	mathematical expressions of each cited statement and its proof are the
    11	same in both up to whitespace and braces (script check recorded in
    12	`provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).
    13	
    14	## Scope
    15	
    16	- The "What it states" column is a faithful paraphrase, sometimes
    17	  shortened. The exact statement is the Lean type in
    18	  `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean`; `Audit/<module>/` prints the
    19	  elaborated types.
    20	- The rows cover every public theorem (82) and the 6 definitions whose
    21	  values are stated as facts. The other 37 public definitions (for example
    22	  `kappa`, `delta`, `gauge`, `counts`) only name quantities used in those
    23	  statements and have no rows of their own; read their bodies in the Lean
    24	  source or in `Audit/`.
    25	- The package checks finite, algebraic and scalar steps only: exact
    26	  identities, polynomial and rational certificates, real-power bookkeeping,
    27	  parameter ranges, and a few finite-dimensional inner-product and
    28	  finite-word facts.
    29	- The SPDE itself, stochastic integrals, Gaussian measures, Fourier and
    30	  spectral analysis, operator theory and all limits in time or in a
    31	  regularization are outside Lean. Where a Lean statement needs an analytic
    32	  fact about the model, that fact enters as an explicit hypothesis of the
    33	  theorem (a "supplied hypothesis" below). Lean checks the deduction from
    34	  those hypotheses, not the hypotheses themselves.
    35	- A successful `lake build` is not a verification receipt for the
    36	  manuscript. It shows that the stated Lean theorems are proved from their
    37	  hypotheses; whether a statement matches the manuscript step it is listed
    38	  against is a separate, human judgment recorded in this ledger.
    39	- Three further modules developed alongside these (normalized Gaussian
    40	  coordinates, vector Gaussian projection, and colored vector words) are
    41	  withheld from this package because they depend on a library that is not
    42	  yet public.
    43	- "no direct label" means the declaration checks a computation from the
    44	  development of the manuscript that does not appear as, or inside, a
    45	  labeled statement of the revision cited above. Such rows make no claim
    46	  about the manuscript.

   135	## DimensionalMatrix
   136	
   137	Defines the backward, coupling and forward 2x2 phase matrices of a single
   138	interaction and computes their product with all four entries retained, in
   139	unweighted coordinates. At fixed frequencies `r`, `rho` the matrices are
   140	the factors of `S(-t) B(b) S(t)` in `E:variance-physical-adjoint` of
   141	`P:actual-wave-form` (`backward` = `S(-t)`, `coupling` = the force
   142	`B(b)(u, v) = (0, b u)`, `forward` = `S(t)`, with `cp = cos(rt)`,
   143	`sp/p = sin(rt)/r` and the coefficient `H` in place of `b`), and
   144	`full_interaction` is that unweighted product. It is not yet the normalized
   145	kernel `E:variance-normalized-kernel`: there `b_r = <r> sin(rt)/r`

   147	change of coordinates on the phase space `E` together with the weight
   148	`1/sqrt(<xi><eta>)`. That conversion, the Fourier interpretation and the
   149	zero-frequency case (where the manuscript uses the continuous sine quotient)
   150	are outside Lean. The free matrix also appears in the proof of

1	\section{The Gaussian operator path}
     2	\label{S:actual-operator-driver}
     3	
     4	We now construct the integrated operator path in the interaction representation
     5	on the same probability space as the original noise. Retain
     6	Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, set $a = \alpha_0$, $s = 1/2$ and $E_r =
     7	H^r(\R^d)\times H^{r-1}(\R^d)$, and initially use real phases $E = E_s$. Let
     8	$H_W$ be the real completion of $C_c^\infty((0,\infty)\times\R^d)$ modulo its
     9	covariance-null tests. The given isonormal process on it is $W$. If $\Gamma =
    10	0$, the operator path and all covariance forms are zero, so the conclusions
    11	below hold directly. Assume $\Gamma \ne 0$ in the construction.
    12	
    13	Choose and fix $R,T > 0$ and a real even nonnegative $\zeta \in
    14	C_c^\infty(\R^d)$ equal to one on $B_1$ and zero off $B_2$. The physical mask is
    15	$\zeta_R(x) = \zeta(x/R)$. The free group $S(t)$ and forms $\ell_R$ are those of
    16	Section~\ref{S:wave-variance}; both phase entries and the continuous
    17	zero-frequency sine quotient are retained. Fix parameters
    18	\begin{equation}\label{E:driver-parameters}
    19	  0<\gamma<\min\left(\frac12,\frac{2-\alpha}{2}\right),\qquad
    20	  \frac12<\theta<\beta<\min\left(1-\frac a2,
    21	  \frac{3-a-\alpha}{2}\right).
    22	\end{equation}
    23	The strict intervals are nonempty. The $C^\theta$ norm is the supremum norm plus
    24	the $\theta$-H\"older seminorm.
    25	
    26	\begin{proposition}[Compact operator path on the original noise space]\label{P:actual-operator-driver}
    27	  There is an orthonormal basis $\{f_j\}$ of $H_W$ with real smooth compact test
    28	  representatives, independent standard real Gaussians $g_j = W(f_j)$, and
    29	  deterministic operators $A_j(0,t)$ on $E$ such that
    30	  \begin{equation}\label{E:driver-path-convergence}
    31	    X_N(t):=\sum_{j\le N}g_jA_j(0,t)\longrightarrow M_R(t)
    32	    \quad\text{in }L^p(\Omega;C^\theta([0,T];\mathcal{B}(E)))
    33	  \end{equation}
    34	  for every finite $p \ge 1$. The limit is a centered Gaussian path on the
    35	  original probability space, starts at zero, and has compact values at every
    36	  time on one probability-one path set. For each fixed real Schwartz pair $z,w$
    37	  and $t \in [0,T]$,
    38	  \begin{equation}\label{E:driver-raw-row}
    39	    \langle M_R(t)z,w\rangle_E=\ell_R((0,t);z,w)
    40	    \quad\text{in }L^2(\Omega).
    41	  \end{equation}
    42	  For long intervals, use the completed covariance test, equivalently the
    43	  additive unit-interval construction justified below. Different compact smooth
    44	  test bases give indistinguishable paths on the same $W$. For constants $C,c >
    45	  0$ depending on the fixed data but not the basis or $p$,
    46	  \begin{equation}\label{E:driver-gaussian-norm}
    47	    (\E\|M_R\|_{C^\theta}^p)^{1/p}\le C\sqrt p,\qquad
    48	    \E\exp(c\|M_R\|_{C^\theta}^2)<\infty.
    49	  \end{equation}
    50	  Its complexification has the corresponding sesquilinear covariance identity.
    51	  Fixed-interval Schatten moments hold at the admissible even indices
    52	  in~\eqref{E:driver-fixed-schatten}. Arbitrary $p$ above refers to
    53	  $\mathcal{B}(E)$, not arbitrary Schatten indices or a Schatten-valued path.
    54	\end{proposition}
    55	
    56	\subsection{A test basis and explicit covariance coefficients}
    57	
    58	\begin{lemma}[Basis in the prescribed quotient]\label{L:driver-noise-basis}
    59	  The nonzero space $H_W$ is separable and infinite-dimensional. It has a real
    60	  orthonormal basis with compact smooth representatives, whose evaluations by
    61	  $W$ are independent standard real Gaussians.
    62	\end{lemma}
    63	
    64	\begin{proof}
    65	  For tests supported in $[0,L]\times K$, with $K$ compact, the physical
    66	  covariance and the temporal Schur bound give the absolute estimate
    67	  \begin{equation}\label{E:driver-test-continuity}
    68	    |\langle F,G\rangle_{H_W}|
    69	    \le |K|\Gamma(K-K)\frac{2L^{1-a}}{1-a}
    70	    \|\|F(t)\|_\infty\|_{L^2(0,L)}
    71	    \|\|G(t)\|_\infty\|_{L^2(0,L)}.
    72	  \end{equation}
    73	  Only spatial differences in $K-K$ contribute. On each rational compact box
    74	  inside positive time, rational step approximations followed by compact smooth
    75	  mollifiers at rational scales give a countable uniformly dense test
    76	  collection, supported in a fixed slightly larger box. The estimate proves
    77	  noise-norm approximation. The union over increasing boxes is dense in the test
    78	  completion. This proves separability without assuming the covariance form is
    79	  injective.
    80	
    81	  Choose $L \ge 1$ with $0 < \Gamma(B_L) < \infty$ and nonnegative compact
    82	  smooth $q \ge 1$ on $B_{2L+1}$. Then
    83	  \[
    84	    Q_{\rm sp}:=\int\Gamma(\ud y)\int q(x)q(x-y)\ud x
    85	    \ge |B_{L+1}|\Gamma(B_L)>0,
    86	  \]
    87	  and the compact-support estimate makes it finite. For every real compact
    88	  smooth positive-time $\tau$, the tensor identity is
    89	  \[
    90	    \|\tau\otimes q\|_{H_W}^2=Q_{\rm sp}\|\tau\|_a^2.
    91	  \]
    92	  Here the temporal norm is computed on any finite interval containing the
    93	  support of $\tau$. It is strictly positive for signed nonzero $\tau$. Indeed,
    94	  zero-extend this deterministic test and use the positive Laplace factorization
    95	  from Lemma~\ref{L:masked-time-completion} to write
    96	  \begin{align*}
    97	    \|\tau\|_a^2
    98	    &=\frac1{\Gamma_E(a)}\int_0^\infty\lambda^{a-1}
    99	    E_\lambda(\tau)\ud\lambda,\\
   100	    E_\lambda(\tau)
   101	    &=\int_\R 2\lambda\left|\int_r^\infty
   102	    e^{-\lambda(t-r)}\tau(t)\ud t\right|^2\ud r.
   103	  \end{align*}
   104	  Signed exchanges are absolutely integrable on the test support, by the
   105	  temporal Schur estimate. If the norm vanished, some $\lambda > 0$ would have
   106	  $E_\lambda = 0$. Its inner integral $v(r)$ is continuous and satisfies $v' =
   107	  \lambda v-\tau$. Vanishing almost everywhere makes it identically zero and
   108	  forces $\tau = 0$. Thus, infinitely many linearly independent compact time
   109	  bumps inject into $H_W$ after multiplication by $q$.
   110	
   111	  Apply Gram--Schmidt to a countable dense real test collection, discarding zero
   112	  residuals in the given null quotient. Infinitude gives an infinite basis; each
   113	  representative is a finite linear combination of compact smooth tests. The
   114	  isonormal identity gives $\E g_jg_k = \delta_{jk}$. Joint Gaussian
   115	  characteristic functions then factor, giving independence and unit variances.
   116	  No physical null direction is removed beyond the prescribed quotient, and no
   117	  $H_W$-valued white Gaussian vector is used. This proves
   118	  Lemma~\ref{L:driver-noise-basis}.
   119	\end{proof}
   120	
   121	\begin{lemma}[Covariance coefficients]\label{L:driver-covariance-coefficients}
   122	  For each basis representative put
   123	  \begin{equation}\label{E:driver-covariance-coefficient}
   124	    H_{j,R}(t,x)=\zeta_R(x)\int_{u>0}|t-u|^{-a}
   125	    \int\Gamma(\ud y)f_j(u,x-y)\ud u.
   126	  \end{equation}
   127	  These functions are real smooth on finite time-space compacts, supported
   128	  spatially in $B_{2R}$, with bounded derivatives there. For smooth compact real
   129	  positive-time $F$, and also for the admitted wave tests
   130	  of~\eqref{E:variance-actual-form},
   131	  \begin{equation}\label{E:driver-literal-covariance}
   132	    \E[W_{\mathbb{C}}(\zeta_RF)g_j]
   133	    =\int H_{j,R}(t,x)F(t,x)\ud t\ud x.
   134	  \end{equation}
   135	  The coefficient on $t \ge 0$ depends only on the $H_W$ class of $f_j$.
   136	\end{lemma}
   137	
   138	\begin{proof}
   139	  Extend $f_j$ smoothly by zero in time and substitute $v = t-u$. The unmasked
   140	  expression is $\int_\R |v|^{-a}\int\Gamma(\ud y)f_j(t-v,x-y)\ud v$. On each
   141	  compact $(t,x)$ set, the integrand involves only bounded $v$ and a common
   142	  compact set of $y$. Local Radon mass and local integrability of $|v|^{-a}$
   143	  allow every mixed derivative to move onto the smooth test. Dominated
   144	  integration proves smoothness and the derivative bounds. Multiplication by
   145	  $\zeta_R$ gives the stated support. Zero extension is only of a deterministic
   146	  test; no negative-time noise is introduced.
   147	
   148	  The physical covariance formula and absolute Fubini give
   149	  \eqref{E:driver-literal-covariance} first for real compact tests. The compact
   150	  difference set in $\Gamma$ and integrable temporal singularity justify the
   151	  exchange. For wave tests use the common-support original approximations of
   152	  Proposition~\ref{P:actual-wave-form}, converging in $L^2$ time in the spatial
   153	  supremum norm after masking. The left side converges by noise Cauchy--Schwarz
   154	  and the right side by the coefficient's boundedness on that support. Real and
   155	  imaginary parts give the complex version. If two representatives give the same
   156	  class, their Gaussian difference is zero. Testing the covariance identity
   157	  against every compact smooth $F$ makes the difference of their masked
   158	  coefficients zero as a distribution for $t > 0$. Smoothness, then continuity
   159	  at zero, proves the representative assertion on $t \ge 0$. This proves
   160	  Lemma~\ref{L:driver-covariance-coefficients}.
   161	\end{proof}

   163	\subsection{Gain, adjoints and localization}
   164	
   165	\begin{lemma}[Deterministic coefficient operators]\label{L:driver-gain-localization}
   166	  For $I \subset [0,T]$, the statewise integral
   167	  \begin{equation}\label{E:driver-coefficient-operator}
   168	    A_j(I)z=\int_I S(-t)B(H_{j,R}(t))S(t)z\ud t
   169	  \end{equation}
   170	  satisfies, for every real $r$,
   171	  \begin{equation}\label{E:driver-gain-one}
   172	    \|A_j(I)\|_{\mathcal{B}(E_r,E_{r+1})}
   173	    \le C_{j,r,R,T}|I|.
   174	  \end{equation}
   175	  Its $E_s$ adjoint has the gain $E_{2s-r-1} \to E_{2s-r}$, so both operators
   176	  act from $E_{s-\gamma}$ to $E$. Choose real compact smooth $\chi = 1$ on
   177	  $B_{2R+T+1}$. On every $E_r$,
   178	  \begin{equation}\label{E:driver-actual-localization}
   179	    D_\chi A_j(I)=A_j(I)=A_j(I)D_\chi.
   180	  \end{equation}
   181	  For each fixed Schwartz pair,
   182	  \begin{equation}\label{E:driver-covariance-row}
   183	    \E[g_j\ell_R(I;z,w)]=\langle A_j(I)z,w\rangle_E.
   184	  \end{equation}
   185	\end{lemma}
   186	
   187	\begin{proof}
   188	  The full massless wave is strongly continuous and bounded on every $E_r$ on
   189	  finite time intervals. Its normalized off-diagonal Fourier entries have sizes
   190	  at most $C_T$ and one, respectively; continuity and domination prove the
   191	  strong assertion. Multiplication by $H_{j,R}(t)$ is bounded on every $H^r$,
   192	  continuously in $t$, by weighted Fourier convolution and its compact smooth
   193	  derivative bounds. Hence, $B(H_{j,R}(t)):E_r \to E_{r+1}$ is bounded: its
   194	  second entry is a multiplier of the displacement in $H^r$. The integrand
   195	  in~\eqref{E:driver-coefficient-operator} is strongly continuous with values in
   196	  $E_{r+1}$ for each input in $E_r$, and uniformly bounded in that operator
   197	  norm. Statewise Bochner integration proves~\eqref{E:driver-gain-one},
   198	  including the Lipschitz operator-norm primitive $A_j(0,t)$. Norm continuity of
   199	  $S(t)$ is not needed.
   200	
   201	  Under the $E_s$ pairing, the dual of $E_r$ is isometrically $E_{2s-r}$,
   202	  directly by the two Bessel weights. Dualizing the bound with a gain of one
   203	  derivative therefore gives the asserted adjoint gain. It agrees on Schwartz
   204	  phases with the bounded $E_s$ adjoint. Since $\gamma < 1$, gain one at every
   205	  index implies the two stated maps from $E_{s-\gamma}$ to $E$.
   206	
   207	  For smooth data the free-wave energy on a shrinking ball has nonpositive
   208	  boundary flux: $v\partial_nu-(v^2+|\nabla u|^2)/2 \le 0$. Vanishing initial
   209	  displacement and velocity give zero velocity and gradient in the cone;
   210	  integration of velocity from the zero displacement gives zero displacement
   211	  there as well. Time reversal gives the backward assertion. Thus, both entries
   212	  of $S(\pm t)$ enlarge supports by at most $|t|$. Density and testing against
   213	  compact smooth functions extend this support assertion to Sobolev phases. In
   214	  particular, for input $(1-D_\chi)z$, approximate $z$ by Schwartz phases and
   215	  retain the factor $1-D_\chi$; the approximants vanish on $B_{2R+T+1}$. Their
   216	  free displacement vanishes on $B_{2R}$ throughout $[0,T]$, and the same is
   217	  true in the distributional limit. They contribute nothing to the integral. Its
   218	  output is supported in $B_{2R+T}$, by the support of $H_{j,R}$ and backward
   219	  finite propagation. Since $\chi = 1$ on a neighborhood of this ball, both
   220	  identities in~\eqref{E:driver-actual-localization} follow. This uses both
   221	  entries, not a scalar restart or a positivity theorem.
   222	
   223	  Finally, apply the physical Sobolev pairing
   224	  \eqref{E:variance-physical-adjoint} and~\eqref{E:driver-literal-covariance} to
   225	  the state integral. They give \eqref{E:driver-covariance-row}.
   226	  In~\eqref{E:driver-covariance-coefficient}, the mask is after convolution;
   227	  replacing it by a mask inside $\Gamma*f_j$ would change this identity. This
   228	  proves Lemma~\ref{L:driver-gain-localization}.
   229	\end{proof}

   231	\subsection{Finite variances and first Wiener chaos tails}
   232	
   233	Put $J_0(u,v) = (\Lambda^{1/2}u,\Lambda^{-1/2}v)$, $H_0 = L^2(\R^d;\R^2)$, $a_j
   234	= J_0A_j(I)J_0^{-1}$ and $P_\chi = J_0D_\chi J_0^{-1}$. The operator $D_\gamma =
   235	\operatorname{diag}(\Lambda^{-\gamma},\Lambda^{-\gamma})$ acts on these physical
   236	coordinates. Its two compact envelopes $B_{\rm out},B_{\rm in}$ are those of
   237	Proposition~\ref{P:compact-two-envelopes}, after complexification when Schatten
   238	norms are used. For $I \subset [0,T]$ with $0 < h = |I| \le 1$, set
   239	\begin{equation}\label{E:driver-short-variance-budget}
   240	  b_I=C_T h^{2-a}B_\alpha(h),
   241	\end{equation}
   242	where $C_T$ is the uniform-in-$R$ constant in
   243	Proposition~\ref{P:wave-two-variances}.
   244	
   245	\begin{lemma}[Both variances and their tails]\label{L:driver-actual-variances}
   246	  For every $N$,
   247	  \begin{equation}\label{E:driver-two-variances}
   248	    V_{{\rm out},N}:=\sum_{j\le N}a_ja_j^*\le b_ID_\gamma^2,
   249	    \qquad V_{{\rm in},N}:=\sum_{j\le N}a_j^*a_j\le b_ID_\gamma^2.
   250	  \end{equation}
   251	  The finite families satisfy both localizations by $P_\chi$. There are bounded
   252	  positive limits $V_{{\rm out},\infty},V_{{\rm in},\infty}$ with positive tails
   253	  $T_{{\rm out},N},T_{{\rm in},N} \to 0$ strongly, and
   254	  \begin{equation}\label{E:driver-compact-tail-envelopes}
   255	    T_{{\rm out},N}\le b_IB_{\rm out},\qquad
   256	    T_{{\rm in},N}\le b_IB_{\rm in}.
   257	  \end{equation}
   258	  For each fixed $z \in E_{s-\gamma}$, the real column maps satisfy
   259	  \begin{equation}\label{E:driver-column-expansions}
   260	    m_{R,I}(z)=\sum_jg_jA_j(I)z,\qquad
   261	    n_{R,I}(z)=\sum_jg_jA_j(I)^{*,E}z
   262	    \quad\text{in }L^2(\Omega;E).
   263	  \end{equation}
   264	\end{lemma}
   265	
   266	\begin{proof}
   267	  By~\eqref{E:driver-covariance-row}, for real Schwartz $z,w$,
   268	  \[
   269	    \langle X_N(I)z,w\rangle_E
   270	    =\sum_{j\le N}g_j\E[g_j\ell_R(I;z,w)]
   271	    =\mathcal{P}_N\ell_R(I;z,w),
   272	  \]
   273	  where $\mathcal{P}_N$ is the orthogonal projection in $L^2(\Omega)$ onto the
   274	  span of $g_1,\ldots,g_N$. In particular,
   275	  \[
   276	    \sum_{j\le N}|\langle A_j(I)z,w\rangle_E|^2
   277	    =\E|\langle X_N(I)z,w\rangle_E|^2
   278	    \le\E|\ell_R(I;z,w)|^2.
   279	  \]
   280	  These are projections onto the noise-test basis, not source regularizations.
   281	  The two variance bounds of Proposition~\ref{P:wave-two-variances}, with the
   282	  mean-square columns of Proposition~\ref{P:wave-square-columns}, apply to these
   283	  same covariance forms and the bound~\eqref{E:driver-short-variance-budget}.
   284	
   285	  Choose a real Schwartz orthonormal basis $\{e_k\}$ of $E$. Fix real Schwartz
   286	  $w$. For every finite phase truncation $K$,
   287	  \[
   288	    \begin{split}
   289	      \sum_{k\le K}\sum_{j\le N}
   290	      |\langle A_j(I)e_k,w\rangle_E|^2
   291	      &=\sum_{k\le K}\E|\langle X_N(I)e_k,w\rangle_E|^2\\
   292	      &\le\sum_{k\le K}\E|\ell_R(I;e_k,w)|^2
   293	      \le b_I\|w\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2,
   294	    \end{split}
   295	  \]
   296	  by~\eqref{E:wave-input-variance}. Let $K \to \infty$. Parseval in the phase
   297	  space and nonnegative monotone convergence, with $N$ still finite, give
   298	  \[
   299	    \sum_{j\le N}\|A_j(I)^{*,E}w\|_E^2
   300	    =\E\|X_N(I)^{*,E}w\|_E^2
   301	    \le b_I\|w\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2.
   302	  \]
   303	  Conversely, for fixed real Schwartz $z$, use \eqref{E:wave-output-variance}
   304	  with the output basis varying:
   305	  \[
   306	    \begin{split}
   307	      \sum_{k\le K}\sum_{j\le N}
   308	      |\langle A_j(I)z,e_k\rangle_E|^2
   309	      &=\sum_{k\le K}\E|\langle X_N(I)z,e_k\rangle_E|^2\\
   310	      &\le\sum_{k\le K}\E|\ell_R(I;z,e_k)|^2
   311	      \le b_I\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2.
   312	    \end{split}
   313	  \]
   314	  The same phase Parseval limit gives
   315	  \[
   316	    \sum_{j\le N}\|A_j(I)z\|_E^2
   317	    =\E\|X_N(I)z\|_E^2
   318	    \le b_I\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2.
   319	  \]
   320	  Thus, both directions use their respective Hilbert-Bessel bounds; neither
   321	  follows from retaining only one variance.
   322	
   323	  These inequalities extend at each finite $N$ to the full $E_{s-\gamma}$ input
   324	  space. Indeed, Lemma~\ref{L:driver-gain-localization} gives $A_j:E_{s-\gamma}
   325	  \to E_{s+1-\gamma} \subset E$. Its adjoint gain, at $r = s+\gamma-1$, gives
   326	  the same map for $A_j^{*,E}$. The inclusion holds since $\gamma < 1$.
   327	  Approximate the input by Schwartz phases and pass each of the finitely many
   328	  operator terms to the limit. The resulting constant is still $b_I$,
   329	  independent of $N$; individual $j$-dependent gain constants were not summed.
   330	  Restricting to $E$ and using $\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}} = \|D_\gamma J_0z\|_{H_0}$

331	  gives \eqref{E:driver-two-variances} as two operator quadratic inequalities.
   332	  Both localizations follow from~\eqref{E:driver-actual-localization}. No
   333	  self-adjointness or projection property of $P_\chi$ is assumed.
   334	
   335	  The coordinates of $m_{R,I}(z)$, for Schwartz $z$, are the original covariance
   336	  forms $\ell_R(I;z,e_k)$ and belong to the closed first Wiener chaos $W(H_W)$.
   337	  Their coefficients against $g_j$ are $\langle A_jz,e_k\rangle_E$. Parseval in
   338	  that chaos, followed by Parseval in $E$ and positive Tonelli, gives
   339	  \[
   340	    \sum_j\|A_jz\|_E^2=\E\|m_{R,I}(z)\|_E^2,
   341	    \qquad m_{R,I}(z)=\sum_jg_jA_jz\quad\text{in }L^2(\Omega;E).
   342	  \]
   343	  The same argument for the adjoint column gives the other expansion. Membership
   344	  in this first chaos comes from linear noise tests, not merely Gaussianity. To
   345	  extend to a fixed $E_{s-\gamma}$ input, approximate by Schwartz phases. The
   346	  finite inequalities extend to that space by the gain bounds and have a
   347	  constant uniform in $N$. Apply them to the input difference, then use the
   348	  Schwartz expansion and continuity of $m,n$. This
   349	  proves~\eqref{E:driver-column-expansions} on the full claimed input domain.
   350	
   351	  The convergent positive quadratic sums, restricted to $E$ and transported by
   352	  $J_0$, define the bounded positive operators $V_{\cdot,\infty}$ by
   353	  polarization and Riesz. They retain the bounds $b_ID_\gamma^2$. Their tails
   354	  have quadratic forms tending to zero. Since they are uniformly bounded and
   355	  positive, $\|T_Nv\|^2 \le \|T_N\|\langle T_Nv,v\rangle \to 0$. Passing to the
   356	  limit in the finite localization identities gives
   357	  \[
   358	    V_{{\rm out},\infty}=P_\chi V_{{\rm out},\infty}P_\chi^*,\qquad
   359	    V_{{\rm in},\infty}=P_\chi^*V_{{\rm in},\infty}P_\chi,
   360	  \]
   361	  and the same identities for their tails. Positive congruence applied to $T_N
   362	  \le b_ID_\gamma^2$ proves~\eqref{E:driver-compact-tail-envelopes}.
   363	
   364	  Complexification preserves these statements and constants. The Hilbert norms
   365	  split into real and imaginary squared norms; real operators extend
   366	  isometrically. A real orthonormal basis complexifies to a complex orthonormal
   367	  basis, preserving singular values and multiplicities. The complex column maps
   368	  have the same bounds and sesquilinear row identities. This proves
   369	  Lemma~\ref{L:driver-actual-variances}.
   370	\end{proof}
   371	
   372	\begin{lemma}[Compact domination of positive tails]\label{L:driver-dominated-tails}
   373	  If $0 \le T_N \le B$, with positive compact $B \in S_m$, $m \ge 1$, and $T_N
   374	  \to 0$ weakly, then
   375	  \begin{equation}\label{E:driver-trace-tails}
   376	    \|T_N\|\longrightarrow0,\qquad \operatorname{Tr}T_N^m\longrightarrow0.
   377	  \end{equation}
   378	\end{lemma}
   379	
   380	\begin{proof}
   381	  Choose a finite spectral projection $Q$ of $B$ with $\|(1-Q)B(1-Q)\| <
   382	  \epsilon$. Positive quadratic Cauchy--Schwarz gives, for unit $x$,
   383	  \[
   384	    \langle T_Nx,x\rangle
   385	    \le2\langle T_NQx,Qx\rangle
   386	    +2\langle T_N(1-Q)x,(1-Q)x\rangle
   387	    \le2\|QT_NQ\|+2\epsilon.
   388	  \]
   389	  Weak convergence makes the finite-dimensional matrix $QT_NQ$ converge in norm
   390	  to zero. Letting $\epsilon\downarrow0$ proves norm convergence.
   391	  Lemma~\ref{L:compact-positive-order} gives $\lambda_j(T_N) \le \lambda_j(B)$,

   540	  $\|K_\chi\|_{S_q} \le \|K_\chi\|_{S_{q_0}}$: if the latter is nonzero,
   541	  normalize by it, so every singular value is at most one, and sum its $q$th
   542	  powers. The zero case is immediate. Apply the finite Gaussian operator
   543	  estimate with the time-refined variances from

   548	    \le C\sqrt q\,|t-u|^\beta,\qquad |t-u|\le1.

   551	  $q$. Longer increments are finite sums of unit increments, with constants
   552	  depending on $T$.

   555	  \le k \le 2^n$. At fine levels $T2^{-n} \le 1$, the elementary bound for a
   556	  finite maximum yields
   557	  \[
   558	    \|D_n(X_N)\|_{L^q}

   562	  are controlled by unit partitions. Minkowski and a geometric sum therefore

    25	\begin{lemma}[Fractional covariance products]
    26	  \label{L:cameron-fractional-products}
    27	  For $\alpha/4 < s < 1/2$, products of real $H^s$ functions define elements of
    28	  $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$, with
    29	  \begin{equation}\label{E:cameron-fractional-product}
    30	    \|fg\|_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}
    31	    \le C_s^2\sqrt{R_{\mathrm{sp}}}\|f\|_{H^s}\|g\|_{H^s}.
    32	  \end{equation}
    33	  Their Hilbert pairings equal their physical integrals. In particular,
    34	  \begin{equation}\label{E:cameron-fractional-absolute}
    35	    \int|f_1(x)f_2(x)f_3(x-y)f_4(x-y)|\ud x\,\Gamma(\ud y)
    36	    \le C_s^4R_{\mathrm{sp}}\prod_{j=1}^4\|f_j\|_{H^s}.
    37	  \end{equation}
    38	\end{lemma}

    42	  four-linear bound~\eqref{E:spatial-four-linear} and covariance PSD make their
    43	  products Cauchy in $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$, with norm at most
    44	  $\sqrt{R_{\mathrm{sp}}}N(f)N(g)$. Expanding product differences proves
    45	  independence of approximation; physical continuity identifies all pairings.
    46	  PSD for products also follows from $fg = ((f+g)^2-(f-g)^2)/4$.
    47	
    48	  Use real radial Fourier bands $D_0 = 1_{\{|\xi|<1\}}$ and $D_j =
    49	  1_{\{2^{j-1}\le|\xi|<2^j\}}$, $j \ge 1$. For $f \in H^s$ put $f_j = D_jf$.
    50	  Each block is real and in $H^1$. Frequency support, Parseval and weighted
    51	  Cauchy--Schwarz give
    52	  \begin{equation}\label{E:cameron-dyadic-product}
    53	    N(f_j)\le2^{j\alpha/4}\|f_j\|_2,\qquad
    54	    \sum_{j\ge0}N(f_j)\le C_s\|f\|_{H^s}.

    58	  result is used. Also $\sum_j\|f_j\|_2 < \infty$ since $s > 0$. Thus,
    59	  $\sum_j|f_j|$ lies in $L^2$ by Minkowski and monotone convergence, and the
    60	  series is absolutely convergent a.e. with sum $f$.
    61	
    62	  Apply the absolute $H^1$ four-linear estimate to each band quadruple. The sum
    63	  of its absolute integrals is at most
    64	  $R_{\mathrm{sp}}\prod_{\ell=1}^4\sum_jN((f_\ell)_j) < \infty$. Tonelli and the

    66	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair} identify the physical product series,

   118	  column is finite rank, and the instantaneous $c_2$ column is zero. Thus, the
   119	  smooth images lie in $\mathcal{K}(F)$, and so does the bounded extension by
   120	  operator-norm closure.

   122	  Choose a complete smooth-test orthonormal basis of $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ by
   123	  countable compact-support approximation and Gram--Schmidt, omitting null
   124	  classes. Let $Q_n$ project onto its first $n$ terms. The row identity yields
   125	  \[
   126	    \|T_{\mathrm{sp}}(I-Q_n)\|
   127	    \le\sup_{k\in\mathcal{L}}\|(I-Q_n)k\|_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}
   128	    \longrightarrow0.
   129	  \]

   131	  finite-net argument and $\|I-Q_n\| \le 1$. Each $T_{\mathrm{sp}}Q_n$ has
   132	  finite-dimensional range; their operator-norm limit is a compact map. This is
   133	  compactness of the map, in addition to compact values. This proves
   134	  Proposition~\ref{P:cameron-spatial-map}.

   139	\begin{lemma}[Supported original tensor space]\label{L:cameron-supported-tensor}
   140	  Canonically $H = H_t\otimes H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ as real Hilbert spaces. It is
   141	  separable and admits a complete orthonormal basis $e_j$ with smooth test
   142	  representatives supported inside $I\times\R^d$. Projection $P_J$ onto its
   143	  first $J$ elements is also an orthogonal projection on $H_W$ by the same

   153	  original covariance norm at most

   156	    \int_I\int_I|s-t|^{-a}\ud s\ud t<\infty.

   161	  completeness; its finite orthonormal projection formula remains orthogonal

   163	  of disjoint time intervals. This proves

   167	\begin{proposition}[The compact temporal mean, without trace class]
   168	  \label{P:cameron-temporal-map}
   169	  Let $K$ on $L^2(I)$ have kernel $|s-t|^{-a}$. It is compact, self-adjoint,
   170	  strictly positive and injective. The map $\iota:f\mapsto K^{1/2}f$ extends
   171	  isometrically from $H_t$ onto $L^2(I)$, and the temporal mean
   172	  \begin{equation}\label{E:cameron-temporal-map}
   173	    C_t=K^{1/2}\iota:H_t\longrightarrow L^r(I)
   174	  \end{equation}
   175	  is bounded and compact for every $2 < r < 2/a$. The displayed formula first
   176	  has its $L^2(I)$ meaning; the same completed map is then shown to take values
   177	  compactly in $L^r(I)$. The operator $K$ is not trace class and $C_t:H_t \to
   178	  L^2(I)$ is not Hilbert--Schmidt.
   179	\end{proposition}
   180	
   181	\begin{proof}
   182	  Schur bounds $K$ by its finite row and column integrals. The Gamma
   183	  representation of $|s-t|^{-a}$ and zero extension of $f \in L^2(I)$ give
   184	  strict positivity directly: the kernel $e^{-\lambda|v|}$ has quadratic form
   185	  \[
   186	    \int_\R\frac{2\lambda}{\lambda^2+\xi^2}
   187	    |\widehat{f}(\xi)|^2\ud\xi>0
   188	    \quad(f\ne0,\ \lambda>0)
   189	  \]
   190	  in the unitary Fourier convention. Absolute Fubini is justified by Schur
   191	  applied to $|f(s)f(t)|$. Integrating with positive weight
   192	  $\lambda^{a-1}/\Gamma_E(a)$ proves positivity and injectivity. Symmetry gives
   193	  self-adjointness. The deterministic truncated kernel $K_\epsilon =
   194	  K1_{\{|s-t|\ge\epsilon\}}$ is square integrable, so finite separated-kernel
   195	  approximations make it compact. The Schur norm of $K-K_\epsilon$ is at most
   196	  $2\epsilon^{1-a}/(1-a)$, proving compactness of $K$. These truncations are not
   197	  used as Gaussian covariances. Its positive square root is compact by the
   198	  compact spectral theorem.
   199	
   200	  On tests $\|K^{1/2}f\|_2 = \|f\|_{H_t}$. Smooth-test $L^2$ density and $\ker K
   201	  = 0$ imply that its range is dense, so the isometry extends onto $L^2(I)$. On
   202	  tests $C_tf = Kf$, and~\eqref{E:cameron-temporal-map} first gives compactness
   203	  into $L^2$.
   204	
   205	  Extend $K_a(v) = |v|^{-a}1_{\{|v|\le1\}}$ to the line. It lies in $L^{r/2}$.
   206	  Scalar Young convolution gives
   207	  \[
   208	    \|g\|_{H_t}^2\le\|K_a\|_{r/2}\|g\|_{r'}^2,\qquad
   209	    r'=r/(r-1).
   210	  \]
   211	  To verify the needed Young inequality, take $u = r/2$, $v = r'$, so $u,v < r$
   212	  and $1/u+1/v = 1+1/r$. Split the absolute convolution integrand into
   213	  $(|f|^u|h|^v)^{1/r}$, $|f|^{1-u/r}$ and $|h|^{1-v/r}$. H\"older with exponents
   214	  $r$, $(1/u-1/r)^{-1}$ and $(1/v-1/r)^{-1}$, followed by integration and
   215	  Tonelli, gives $\|f*h\|_r \le \|f\|_u\|h\|_v$. Covariance Cauchy--Schwarz and
   216	  $L^r$ duality now imply $\|Kf\|_r \le C_{a,r}\|f\|_{H_t}$ on tests. Their $Kf$
   217	  are bounded by the integrable-kernel row, making duality legitimate before
   218	  completion. Density extends the estimate, with $L^2$ value equal
   219	  to~\eqref{E:cameron-temporal-map}. Choose $r < r_2 < 2/a$. Compactness into
   220	  $L^2$ and boundedness into $L^{r_2}$ give compactness into $L^r$ by $\|u\|_r
   221	  \le \|u\|_2^\tau\|u\|_{r_2}^{1-\tau}$ with $1/r = \tau/2+(1-\tau)/r_2$.
   222	
   223	  Finally, the orthonormal cell indicators $N^{1/2}1_{(j/N,(j+1)/N)}$, $0 \le j
   224	  < N$, have $K$ quadratic forms summing to $2N^a/((1-a)(2-a)) \to \infty$.
   225	  Thus, positive $K$ has infinite trace, and $K^{1/2}\iota$ is not
   226	  Hilbert--Schmidt into $L^2$. No instantaneous $L^2$-valued Gaussian has been
   227	  introduced. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:cameron-temporal-map}.
   228	\end{proof}

   230	\begin{proposition}[The compact time-space mean]\label{P:cameron-full-mean}

231	  Fix one $2 < r < 2/a$ throughout this proposition. For finite tensors with
   232	  orthonormal spatial labels define
   233	  \[
   234	    \mathcal{U}\left(\sum_j f_j\otimes q_j\right)(s)
   235	    =\sum_j(Kf_j)(s)q_j.
   236	  \]
   237	  It extends to a bounded map $H \to L^r(I;H_{\mathrm{sp}})$ with dimension-free
   238	  bound. The map
   239	  \begin{equation}\label{E:cameron-full-mean}
   240	    T\Phi(s)=T_{\mathrm{sp}}(\mathcal{U}\Phi(s))
   241	    :H\longrightarrow L^r(I;\mathcal{K}(F))
   242	  \end{equation}
   243	  is compact. For smooth supported $\Phi$, it is the multiplier
   244	  $iB_F(m_Rh_\Phi(s))$, where $h_\Phi = |\cdot|^{-a}*(\Gamma*\Phi)$. For the
   245	  supported projections of Lemma~\ref{L:cameron-supported-tensor},
   246	  \begin{equation}\label{E:cameron-compact-tail}
   247	    \epsilon_J:=\|T(I-P_J)\|_{H\to L^r(\mathcal{K}(F))}
   248	    \longrightarrow0.
   249	  \end{equation}
   250	\end{proposition}
   251	
   252	\begin{proof}
   253	  For a finite-dimensional spatial field $g$, positivity of the time kernel and
   254	  scalar Young give
   255	  \[
   256	    \|g\|_{H_t\otimes H_{\mathrm{sp}}}^2
   257	    \le\int_I\int_I|s-t|^{-a}\|g_s\|\|g_t\|\ud s\ud t
   258	    \le C_{a,r}^2\|g\|_{L^{r'}(H_{\mathrm{sp}})}^2.
   259	  \]

   261	  $\|\mathcal{U}\Phi\|_{L^r(H_{\mathrm{sp}})} \le C_{a,r}\|\Phi\|_H$. The
   262	  duality can be checked by the pointwise direction
   263	  $\|\mathcal{U}\Phi\|^{r-2}\mathcal{U}\Phi$ and smooth coefficient
   264	  approximation in $L^{r'}$, controlled by the displayed estimate. No dimension
   265	  factor occurs. Tensor density and completeness extend this to a strongly
   266	  measurable Bochner field. This time-only map still contains spatial vectors in
   267	  the covariance space. Spatial covariance is applied once, by
   268	  $T_{\mathrm{sp}}$.
   269	
   270	  The physical mean identity on separated tests follows
   271	  from~\eqref{E:cameron-spatial-row}. For a smooth spacetime test use the
   272	  separated compact-support approximations in the tensor proof. Their uniform
   273	  errors give uniformly small masked mean errors, using the finite time row and
   274	  locally finite spatial covariance on the relevant compact differences. The
   275	  multiplier bound by $L^\infty+L^2$ then gives uniform operator convergence,
   276	  identifying the $L^r$ mean in~\eqref{E:cameron-full-mean}. General $H$
   277	  controls denote completed operator fields, without a pointwise-potential
   278	  assertion.
   279	
   280	  Let $Q_n$ be the spatial projections in the compact-map proof. The maps
   281	  $T_n\Phi = T_{\mathrm{sp}}Q_n\mathcal{U}\Phi$ approximate $T$ in operator norm
   282	  by the dimension-free bound and $\|T_{\mathrm{sp}}(I-Q_n)\| \to 0$. For fixed

   298	
   299	Choose integer $B \ge 1$ and $0 < \delta < \min(1,1/B)$. Put $N =
   300	\lfloor1/(\delta B)\rfloor$, $s_m = m\delta B$, $\ell_m = B$ for $m < N$ and
   301	$\ell_N = \delta^{-1}-NB \in [0,B)$. The intervals $I_m =
   302	[s_m,s_m+\delta\ell_m]$ partition $[0,1]$ up to endpoints. With $Q_J = I-P_J$ on
   303	$H_W$ and the explicit pullback~\eqref{E:raw-block-pullback}, define
   304	\[
   305	  Y_{m,J}(f)=W(Q_JT_{\delta,m}f),\qquad
   306	  g_\delta=\delta^{(1-a)/2}.

   309	\begin{equation}\label{E:cameron-block-parameters}
   310	  \frac12<\theta<\min\left(1-\frac a2,\frac{3-a-\alpha}{2}\right),
   311	  \qquad \frac1{1-\theta}<r<\frac2a,\qquad
   312	  \frac1\theta\le p<2<r .

   314	These intervals are nonempty.

   316	\begin{lemma}[Supported residual paths]\label{L:cameron-actual-residual}
   317	  Gaussian transfer with mask $m_R$ and its $F$ extension constructs the
   318	  centered Gaussian paths
   319	  \[
   320	    X_{m,J}(u)=g_\delta A_{m_R}(Y_{m,J})(\min(u,\ell_m)),
   321	    \qquad 0\le u\le B.
   322	  \]

   324	  $\mathscr{B}_0 = h_0^\theta([0,B];\mathcal{K}(F))$. Every continuous linear
   325	  statistic $\ell(X)$ is $W(k_\ell)$ for some $k_\ell \in H_I$. An empty last
   326	  interval gives zero.

   329	\begin{proof}
   330	  Isometry of the pullback and orthogonality of $Q_J$ give
   331	  $\operatorname{Var}Y_{m,J}(f) \le \|f\|_{H_W}^2$.
   332	  Proposition~\ref{P:source-gaussian-transfer} therefore applies. Its finite
   333	  sums retain both deterministic localizations, and their limits retain the true
   334	  $F$ extension and constant columns. Choose $\theta < \beta < \beta_2$ below
   335	  the upper threshold in~\eqref{E:cameron-block-parameters}; read the
   336	  operator-path construction at exponent $\beta$ with auxiliary $\beta_2$.
   337	  Constant stopping preserves compact values and $C^\beta$ bounds, hence gives
   338	  paths in the little $C^\theta$ closure by polygonal approximation. Its
   339	  separability is Lemma~\ref{L:raw-block-inputs}.
   340	
   341	  As in Lemma~\ref{L:raw-block-inputs}, every observed row's slow pullback
   342	  belongs to $H_I$: its time support is in $[0,1]$, and approximating its
   343	  indicator inside $I$ converges in original covariance norm by dominated
   344	  convergence against the integrable time kernel and locally finite $\Gamma$ on

   346	  both true constant columns supply the identities, then boundedness extends
   347	  them to $F$. Let $P_H$ be the orthogonal projection onto closed $H_I$.

   349	  row unchanged, since its residual slow test already lies in $H_I$. Countable

   358	\begin{proposition}[Cameron covariance and averaged bound]
   359	  \label{P:cameron-actual-embedding}
   360	  The covariance map $L_{\delta,J}\Phi = \E[XW(\Phi)]$ is
   361	  \begin{equation}\label{E:cameron-actual-covariance}
   362	    (L_{\delta,J}\Phi)_m(u)=\sqrt\delta
   363	    \int_0^{\min(u,\ell_m)}
   364	    S_F(-v)T(Q_J\Phi)(s_m+\delta v)S_F(v)\ud v ,
   365	    \qquad \Phi\in H.
   366	  \end{equation}
   367	  This is a compact-operator Bochner integral. Define the exact norm and
   368	  constants
   369	  \begin{equation}\label{E:cameron-averaged-norm}
   370	    \|x\|_{\delta,p}
   371	    =\left(\delta\sum_{m=0}^N\|x_m\|_{C^\theta}^p\right)^{1/p},
   372	    \quad G_B=\sup_{|v|\le B}\|S_F(v)\|,
   373	    \quad C_B=G_B^2[B^{1-1/r}+B^{1-1/r-\theta}].
   374	  \end{equation}
   375	  Then the Gaussian Cameron embedding satisfies
   376	  \begin{equation}\label{E:cameron-averaged-bound}
   377	    \|L_{\delta,J}\Phi\|_{\delta,p}
   378	    \le\sqrt\delta\,C_B(2/B)^{1/p-1/r}
   379	    \epsilon_J\|\Phi\|_H .
   380	  \end{equation}
   381	  Convergence $\epsilon_J \to 0$ fixes $R$ and is independent of $\delta$.
   382	\end{proposition}
   383	
   384	\begin{proof}
   385	  For smooth supported $\Phi$, $Q_J\Phi$ is another such test. The explicit
   386	  pullback covariance~\eqref{E:raw-block-mean-jacobian} gives
   387	  \[
   388	    \E[Y_{m,J}(f)W(\Phi)]
   389	    =\delta^{a/2}\int f(v,x)
   390	    h_{Q_J\Phi}(s_m+\delta v,x)\ud x\ud v .
   391	  \]
   392	  Absolute Fubini also holds for signed compact tests. Multiplying by $g_\delta$
   393	  gives $\sqrt\delta$. Explicit rows and~\eqref{E:cameron-spatial-row} give
   394	  \eqref{E:cameron-actual-covariance}. The constant-velocity input acquires
   395	  displacement $v$ under $S_F(v)$; the constant displacement remains one. Both
   396	  columns are included.
   397	
   398	  Both $S_F$ and its adjoint are strongly continuous on Hilbert $F$. In
   399	  Bessel-unitary $E$ coordinates the Fourier matrix is
   400	  \[
   401	    \begin{pmatrix}
   402	      \cos(v|\xi|)&\langle\xi\rangle\sin(v|\xi|)/|\xi|\\
   403	      -|\xi|\sin(v|\xi|)/\langle\xi\rangle&\cos(v|\xi|)
   404	    \end{pmatrix}.

   408	  finite dimensional. For compact $A$, conjugation $S_F(-v)AS_F(v)$ is norm
   409	  continuous: strong convergence is uniform on compact images, and the right
   410	  factor follows by adjoints. Joint norm continuity in $(v,A)$ and uniform

   412	  compact-operator field. No norm continuity of the free group itself is
   413	  assumed.
   414	
   415	  Write $M = TQ_J\Phi$. H\"older and the primitive increment estimate give
   416	  \begin{equation}\label{E:cameron-local-primitive-bound}
   417	    \|(L_{\delta,J}\Phi)_m\|_{C^\theta}
   418	    \le\sqrt\delta\,C_B\delta^{-1/r}\|M\|_{L^r(I_m)}.

   446	    \|L_{\delta,J}\Phi\|_{\delta,p}

1	\section{Finite Gaussian moments and whole-space Sobolev compactness}
     2	\label{S:compact-gaussian}
     3	
     4	We prove the finite Gaussian and compact-cutoff estimates needed to construct
     5	the wave operator path. All traces and Schatten norms in this section are
     6	unnormalized. The spatial states remain on $\R^d$, $d \in \{1,2,3\}$. Here $p$
     7	is an auxiliary Schatten and Gaussian-moment index. The auxiliary periodic space
     8	below is used only to factor a compactly supported multiplication operator. No
     9	infinite Gaussian series or time path is constructed in this section.
    10	
    11	\subsection{Finite Gaussian matrices with both variance powers}
    12	
    13	\begin{lemma}[Scalar power estimates]\label{L:gaussian-scalar-powers}
    14	  For $0 < \theta < 1$ and $u,v \ge 0$,
    15	  \begin{equation}\label{E:gaussian-weighted-power}
    16	    u^\theta v^{1-\theta} \le \theta u+(1-\theta)v.
    17	  \end{equation}
    18	  Consequently, if $L > 0$ and $0 \le q \le L$ are integers, then for real
    19	  $x,y$,
    20	  \begin{equation}\label{E:gaussian-integer-power}
    21	    |x|^q|y|^{L-q}
    22	    \le \frac qL|x|^L+\frac{L-q}L|y|^L.
    23	  \end{equation}
    24	  For nonnegative finite sequences, the usual H\"older inequality holds with
    25	  exponents $m$ and $m/(m-1)$, $m > 1$. If $Z \ge 0$ has finite expectation $F$
    26	  and $0 < r < 1$, then $\E Z^r \le F^r$.
    27	\end{lemma}
    28	
    29	\begin{proof}
    30	  If $v > 0$, divide~\eqref{E:gaussian-weighted-power} by $v$ and put $t = u/v$.
    31	  The function $\theta t+1-\theta-t^\theta$ decreases to zero at one and then
    32	  increases, by its derivative $\theta(1-t^{\theta-1})$. Continuity covers $t =
    33	  0$; if $v = 0$ the inequality is immediate. For $0 < q < L$, apply this with
    34	  $u = |x|^L$, $v = |y|^L$ and $\theta = q/L$. The endpoint cases $q = 0,L$ are
    35	  identities, with the ordinary integer convention $a^0 = 1$.
    36	
    37	  To prove finite H\"older, divide the two sequences by their respective
    38	  $\ell^m$ and $\ell^{m/(m-1)}$ norms. If either norm vanishes, the result is
    39	  immediate. Apply~\eqref{E:gaussian-weighted-power} with $\theta = 1/m$ to the
    40	  corresponding normalized powers and sum; the sum of products is at most one.
    41	  Undo the normalization. Finally, $F = 0$ gives $Z = 0$ almost surely. If $F >
    42	  0$, apply \eqref{E:gaussian-weighted-power} to $u = Z/F$, $v = 1$ and $\theta
    43	  = r$, and integrate. The right side has expectation one. This proves
    44	  Lemma~\ref{L:gaussian-scalar-powers}.
    45	\end{proof}
    46	
    47	\begin{lemma}[Two Hermitian trace bounds]\label{L:gaussian-trace-bounds}
    48	  Let $B,Y$ be finite Hermitian matrices, $m \ge 2$ an integer, and $L = 2m-2$.
    49	  For integers $0 \le q \le L$,
    50	  \begin{equation}\label{E:gaussian-trace-word}
    51	    \operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}(BY^qBY^{L-q})
    52	    \le \operatorname{Tr}(B^2|Y|^L).
    53	  \end{equation}
    54	  If $D \ge 0$ is Hermitian, then
    55	  \begin{equation}\label{E:gaussian-trace-holder}
    56	    \operatorname{Tr}(D|Y|^{2m-2})
    57	    \le (\operatorname{Tr}D^m)^{1/m}
    58	    (\operatorname{Tr}|Y|^{2m})^{(m-1)/m}.
    59	  \end{equation}
    60	\end{lemma}
    61	
    62	\begin{proof}
    63	  Diagonalize $Y$, with real eigenvalues $\lambda_i$, and write $b_{ij}$ for the
    64	  entries of $B$ in that basis. Hermitian symmetry gives $b_{ji} =
    65	  \overline{b_{ij}}$. The trace word is the real sum
    66	  \[
    67	    \sum_{i,j}|b_{ij}|^2\lambda_j^q\lambda_i^{L-q}.
    68	  \]
    69	  Bound each product by its absolute value and use
    70	  \eqref{E:gaussian-integer-power}. After interchanging $i,j$, the two resulting
    71	  sums agree because $|b_{ij}| = |b_{ji}|$. Each equals
    72	  $\sum_{i,j}|b_{ij}|^2|\lambda_i|^L = \operatorname{Tr}(B^2|Y|^L)$. The two
    73	  weights sum to one, proving \eqref{E:gaussian-trace-word}. No commutation of
    74	  $B$ and $Y$ is used.
    75	
    76	  In the same basis put $d_i = D_{ii} \ge 0$. If $\theta_j$ are the nonnegative
    77	  eigenvalues of $D$, a unitary change of basis gives $d_i =
    78	  \sum_j|U_{ij}|^2\theta_j$. Both row and column sums of $|U_{ij}|^2$ equal one.
    79	  Finite convexity therefore yields
    80	  \[
    81	    \sum_i d_i^m \le \sum_{i,j}|U_{ij}|^2\theta_j^m
    82	    = \operatorname{Tr}D^m.
    83	  \]
    84	  For completeness, the convexity step follows from $t^m \ge s^m+ms^{m-1}(t-s)$
    85	  for $s,t \ge 0$, obtained by differentiating the difference. Average this
    86	  inequality with $s$ equal to the weighted mean. Now apply finite H\"older from
    87	  Lemma~\ref{L:gaussian-scalar-powers} to $\sum_i d_i|\lambda_i|^{2m-2}$. Since
    88	  $(2m-2)m/(m-1) = 2m$, the last display proves \eqref{E:gaussian-trace-holder},
    89	  including zero sums. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:gaussian-trace-bounds}.
    90	\end{proof}

    92	\begin{proposition}[Finite Gaussian matrix moment]\label{P:finite-gaussian-matrix}
    93	  Let $A_1,\ldots,A_N$ be complex $o$-by-$n$ matrices, with $o,n,N \ge 1$, and
    94	  let $g_k$ be independent real standard Gaussians. Put
    95	  \[
    96	    X=\sum_k g_kA_k,\qquad V_{\rm out}=\sum_k A_kA_k^*,
    97	    \qquad V_{\rm in}=\sum_k A_k^*A_k.
    98	  \]
    99	  For even $p = 2m \ge 2$, with $\|A\|_{S_p}^p = \operatorname{Tr}((A^*A)^m)$,
   100	  \begin{align}
   101	    (\E\|X\|_{S_p}^p)^{1/p}
   102	    &\le \sqrt{p-1}\left(
   103	    \frac{\operatorname{Tr}V_{\rm out}^m+
   104	    \operatorname{Tr}V_{\rm in}^m}{2}\right)^{1/p}
   105	    \label{E:finite-gaussian-average}\\
   106	    &\le \sqrt{p-1}\max\left(
   107	    \|V_{\rm out}^{1/2}\|_{S_p},\|V_{\rm in}^{1/2}\|_{S_p}\right).
   108	    \label{E:finite-gaussian-maximum}
   109	  \end{align}
   110	  The constants are independent of $o,n,N$. The first inequality is an equality
   111	  at $p = 2$. Empty or zero families give the zero identity.
   112	\end{proposition}
   113	
   114	\begin{proof}
   115	  First suppose $B_k$ are Hermitian and put $Y = \sum_k g_kB_k$ and $D = \sum_k
   116	  B_k^2$. All polynomial moments are finite because Gaussian decay dominates
   117	  every fixed power. Componentwise integration by parts against the product
   118	  Gaussian density gives $\E[g_kP(g)] = \E[\partial_kP(g)]$, with zero boundary
   119	  terms. It applies to complex polynomials through their real and imaginary
   120	  parts; absolute polynomial integrability justifies Fubini.
   121	
   122	  For $m \ge 2$, put $F = \E\operatorname{Tr}Y^{2m}$ and $L = 2m-2$. Write
   123	  $\operatorname{Tr}Y^{2m} = \sum_k g_k \operatorname{Tr}(B_kY^{2m-1})$ and
   124	  differentiate the $2m-1$ factors in their order. This gives exactly
   125	  \[
   126	    F=\sum_k\sum_{q=0}^{L}
   127	    \E\operatorname{Tr}(B_kY^qB_kY^{L-q}).
   128	  \]
   129	  The eigenbasis calculation above shows these traces are real. The
   130	  differentiated polynomial is real by conjugation and trace cyclicity. No
   131	  derivative of a spectral absolute value or measurable choice of an eigenbasis
   132	  is needed. The two trace bounds give
   133	  \begin{align*}
   134	    F&\le (2m-1)\E\operatorname{Tr}(D|Y|^{2m-2})\\
   135	    &\le (2m-1)(\operatorname{Tr}D^m)^{1/m}
   136	    \E(\operatorname{Tr}|Y|^{2m})^{(m-1)/m}\\
   137	    &\le (2m-1)(\operatorname{Tr}D^m)^{1/m}F^{(m-1)/m}.
   138	  \end{align*}
   139	  Here $\operatorname{Tr}|Y|^{2m} = \operatorname{Tr}Y^{2m}$, and the last
   140	  inequality is the expectation bound in Lemma~\ref{L:gaussian-scalar-powers}.
   141	  If $F = 0$ the conclusion is immediate. Otherwise divide by its positive
   142	  fractional power and raise to $m$ to obtain
   143	  \begin{equation}\label{E:finite-hermitian-gaussian}
   144	    \E\operatorname{Tr}Y^{2m} \le (2m-1)^m\operatorname{Tr}D^m.
   145	  \end{equation}
   146	  For $m = 1$, independence gives directly $\E\operatorname{Tr}Y^2 =
   147	  \sum_k\operatorname{Tr}B_k^2 = \operatorname{Tr}D$, proving the same formula
   148	  as equality.
   149	
   150	  For rectangular $A_k$, use the Hermitian dilation
   151	  \[
   152	    B_k=\begin{pmatrix}0&A_k\\A_k^*&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
   153	    Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&X\\X^*&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
   154	    D=\operatorname{diag}(V_{\rm out},V_{\rm in}).
   155	  \]
   156	  Finite entrywise summation proves $\operatorname{Tr}(UV) =
   157	  \operatorname{Tr}(VU)$ for compatible rectangular matrices. Since $(XX^*)^m =
   158	  X(X^*X)^{m-1}X^*$, it follows that
   159	  \[
   160	    \operatorname{Tr}Y^{2m}=2\operatorname{Tr}((X^*X)^m),\qquad
   161	    \operatorname{Tr}D^m=\operatorname{Tr}V_{\rm out}^m+
   162	    \operatorname{Tr}V_{\rm in}^m.
   163	  \]
   164	  Substitute in~\eqref{E:finite-hermitian-gaussian}, divide by two and take the
   165	  $p$th root. This proves~\eqref{E:finite-gaussian-average}. For positive $V$,
   166	  spectral diagonalization gives $\|V^{1/2}\|_{S_p}^p = \operatorname{Tr}V^m$,
   167	  and the average of two nonnegative numbers is bounded by their maximum. At $p
   168	  = 2$, $\E\operatorname{Tr}X^*X = \operatorname{Tr}V_{\rm in} =
   169	  \operatorname{Tr}V_{\rm out}$, proving the claimed equality. This proves
   170	  Proposition~\ref{P:finite-gaussian-matrix}.
   171	\end{proof}

   173	\begin{remark}[Both variance directions are necessary]
   174	  \label{R:gaussian-one-variance-test}
   175	  Let $n = 16$ and $A_k = e_k^{\mathsf{T}}$ be the coordinate row matrices. The
   176	  only nonzero singular value of $X$ is $(\sum_k g_k^2)^{1/2}$. Gaussian

   179	    \E\|X\|_{S_4}^4=3n+n(n-1)=n(n+2)=288.
   180	  \]

   183	  $9\operatorname{Tr}I_n^2 = 144$, which is false. Transposing the family
   184	  refutes the corresponding output-only bound. The average and maximum bounds
   185	  have fourth powers $1224$ and $2304$, respectively. This finite example
   186	  asserts nothing about a specialized wave estimate.
   187	\end{remark}

   189	\subsection{Whole-space cutoffs through an auxiliary periodic space}
   190	
   191	Use the unitary Fourier transform with $c_d = (2\pi)^{-d/2}$ and $\Lambda =
   192	(1-\Delta)^{1/2}$. For real $r$, the norm on $H^r(\R^d)$ is
   193	$\|\langle\xi\rangle^r\widehat{u}\|_2$. The deterministic cutoff arguments allow
   194	any smoothing order $\gamma > 0$. Fix real $\sigma$ and a real compact smooth
   195	$\chi$. Singular values $s_j$, $j \ge 1$, are counted with multiplicity, with
   196	zeros appended when necessary. For compact $K$, put $\|K\|_{S_p}^p = \sum_j
   197	s_j(K)^p$.
   198	
   199	\begin{lemma}[Cutoff factorization]\label{L:cutoff-factorization}
   200	  Choose a cube $Q_L = (-L/2,L/2)^d$ containing $\operatorname{supp}\chi$ in its
   201	  interior, and a real $\psi \in C_c^\infty(Q_L)$ equal to one near
   202	  $\operatorname{supp}\chi$. On the auxiliary torus $\mathbb{T}_L$ use Lebesgue
   203	  measure and the orthonormal basis
   204	  \[
   205	    e_k(x)=L^{-d/2}e^{i\kappa_k\cdot x},\qquad
   206	    \kappa_k=2\pi k/L,\qquad k \in \mathbb{Z}^d,
   207	  \]
   208	  with $\|v\|_{H^r(\mathbb{T}_L)}^2 = \sum_k\langle\kappa_k\rangle^{2r}|v_k|^2$.
   209	  Periodization of $\psi u$ and multiplication of a periodic function by $\chi$
   210	  extend to bounded maps
   211	  \begin{equation}\label{E:cutoff-periodic-maps}
   212	    \mathcal{P}_\psi:H^r(\R^d)\to H^r(\mathbb{T}_L),\qquad
   213	    \mathcal{E}_\chi:H^r(\mathbb{T}_L)\to H^r(\R^d)
   214	  \end{equation}
   215	  for every real $r$. If $\mathcal{I}_\gamma$ denotes the identity inclusion
   216	  from $H^{\sigma+\gamma}(\mathbb{T}_L)$ to $H^\sigma(\mathbb{T}_L)$, then
   217	  \begin{equation}\label{E:cutoff-whole-space-recovery}
   218	    \mathcal{E}_\chi\mathcal{I}_\gamma\mathcal{P}_\psi u=\chi u,
   219	    \qquad u \in H^{\sigma+\gamma}(\R^d).
   220	  \end{equation}
   221	\end{lemma}
   222	
   223	\begin{proof}
   224	  For $x,y \in \R^d$ and real $r$, the elementary inequality $\langle x\rangle
   225	  \le \sqrt{2}\langle y\rangle\langle x-y\rangle$ gives
   226	  \begin{equation}\label{E:cutoff-peetre}
   227	    \left(\frac{\langle x\rangle}{\langle y\rangle}\right)^r
   228	    \le 2^{|r|/2}\langle x-y\rangle^{|r|}.
   229	  \end{equation}
   230	  For negative $r$, interchange $x,y$ before raising to $|r|$. Integration by
   231	  parts gives rapid decay of the Fourier transform of every compact smooth
   232	  cutoff. For any lattice spacing $a > 0$ and $N > d$,
   233	  \begin{equation}\label{E:cutoff-lattice-sum}
   234	    \sup_y\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\langle y-ak\rangle^{-N}<\infty.
   235	  \end{equation}
   236	  Indeed, translate $y$ into a centered lattice cell, where $|y| \le a\sqrt
   237	  d/2$. For $|k| \ge \sqrt d$ we have $|y-ak| \ge a|k|/2$. The remaining terms
   238	  are finite; the tail converges by dyadic lattice counting, since there are at
   239	  most $C_d2^{jd}$ lattice points in the $j$th shell in $k$. More precisely, for
   240	  $|k| \ge \sqrt d$, the preceding inequality gives
   241	  \[
   242	    \langle y-ak\rangle^{-N}
   243	    \le \max(1,2/a)^N\langle k\rangle^{-N}.
   244	  \]
   245	  The comparison-series terms are bounded by $2^{-jN}$ on each dyadic $k$-shell.
   246	  Thus, its convergent geometric sum carries constants depending on $a,d,N$, as
   247	  does~\eqref{E:cutoff-lattice-sum}.
   248	
   249	  We use the mixed Schur bound for a kernel whose absolute row and column
   250	  integrals are bounded by $M_1,M_2$. Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz at each output
   251	  point, followed by Tonelli, bounds its squared operator norm by $M_1M_2$. The
   252	  same proof works with counting measure on one side and Lebesgue measure on the
   253	  other, first on dense finite or compact inputs.
   254	
   255	  For Schwartz $u$, the $k$th coefficient of its cutoff periodization is
   256	  \[
   257	    (\mathcal{P}_\psi u)_k
   258	    = L^{-d/2}\int\psi(x)u(x)e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x}\ud x
   259	    = L^{-d/2}\int\widehat{\psi}(\kappa_k-\xi)\widehat{u}(\xi)\ud\xi.
   260	  \]
   261	  The $c_d$ from Fourier inversion cancels the $c_d^{-1}$ in the ordinary
   262	  Fourier integral of $\psi$. After weighting, its exact kernel is
   263	  \[
   264	    L^{-d/2}\left(\frac{\langle\kappa_k\rangle}{\langle\xi\rangle}\right)^r
   265	    \widehat{\psi}(\kappa_k-\xi).
   266	  \]
   267	  For a finite torus polynomial $v$, the normalized Fourier kernel of
   268	  $\mathcal{E}_\chi v$ is
   269	  \[
   270	    L^{-d/2}\left(\frac{\langle\xi\rangle}{\langle\kappa_k\rangle}\right)^r
   271	    \widehat{\chi}(\xi-\kappa_k).
   272	  \]
   273	  There is no additional $c_d$ in this kernel. By~\eqref{E:cutoff-peetre}, each
   274	  is bounded in absolute value by a rapidly decreasing function of its frequency
   275	  difference, times a fixed constant. One Schur quantity is its $L^1$ integral
   276	  and the other a uniformly translated lattice sum, bounded
   277	  by~\eqref{E:cutoff-lattice-sum}. This proves~\eqref{E:cutoff-periodic-maps},
   278	  including negative $r$.
   279	
   280	  Smooth compact approximation in weighted Fourier $L^2$ proves Schwartz density
   281	  on $\R^d$; weighted sequence truncation proves polynomial density on the
   282	  torus. Hence, these maps extend uniquely. Their distributional meanings follow
   283	  by testing against compact smooth functions and density: each periodic
   284	  coefficient pairs the distribution with a compact smooth test. No point
   285	  sampling of a rough Fourier function is used. The same full-Lebesgue Schur
   286	  argument proves smooth compact multiplication bounded on every whole-space
   287	  $H^r$.
   288	
   289	  For Schwartz $u$, the periodic Fourier series of $\psi u$ converges smoothly
   290	  on the cube. Since $\chi\psi = \chi$ and $\chi$ is supported strictly inside
   291	  the cube, multiplying this series by $\chi$ recovers $\chi u$ with no alias
   292	  term. Both sides are bounded from $H^{\sigma+\gamma}(\R^d)$ to
   293	  $H^\sigma(\R^d)$, using the just-proved maps, the inclusion and smooth
   294	  multiplication. Density proves \eqref{E:cutoff-whole-space-recovery} on that
   295	  full domain. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:cutoff-factorization}.
   296	\end{proof}
   297	
   298	\begin{proposition}[Whole-space cutoff singular values]\label{P:cutoff-singular-values}
   299	  For real $\sigma$ and $\gamma > 0$, the initially Schwartz-defined operator
   300	  $K_{\chi,\sigma,\gamma} = \Lambda^\sigma\chi\Lambda^{-\sigma-\gamma}$ extends
   301	  uniquely to a compact operator on $L^2(\R^d)$, and
   302	  \begin{equation}\label{E:cutoff-singular-values}
   303	    s_j(K_{\chi,\sigma,\gamma})
   304	    \le C_{\chi,\sigma,\gamma,d}j^{-\gamma/d},\qquad j \ge 1.
   305	  \end{equation}
   306	  Consequently, $K_{\chi,\sigma,\gamma} \in S_p$ whenever $p \ge 1$ and $p\gamma
   307	  > d$.
   308	\end{proposition}
   309	
   310	\begin{proof}

311	  The zero cutoff is immediate. Fix one cube and cutoff pair $L,\psi$ as in
   312	  Lemma~\ref{L:cutoff-factorization}. Its recovery identity gives
   313	  \[
   314	    K_{\chi,\sigma,\gamma}
   315	    =\Lambda^\sigma\mathcal{E}_\chi\mathcal{I}_\gamma
   316	    \mathcal{P}_\psi\Lambda^{-\sigma-\gamma}.
   317	  \]
   318	  In the weighted torus coordinates, $\mathcal{I}_\gamma$ is diagonal with
   319	  entries $\langle\kappa_k\rangle^{-\gamma}$. Let $Q_n$ retain $|k|_\infty \le
   320	  n$. Its rank is $(2n+1)^d$, and
   321	  \[
   322	    \|(1-Q_n)\mathcal{I}_\gamma\|
   323	    \le [1+(2\pi/L)^2(n+1)^2]^{-\gamma/2}\longrightarrow0.
   324	  \]
   325	  Replacing the inclusion by $Q_n\mathcal{I}_\gamma$ gives finite-rank $K_n$
   326	  converging in norm to $K_{\chi,\sigma,\gamma}$. This proves compactness:
   327	  finite-dimensional images have finite nets of each positive radius, and norm
   328	  approximation transfers those nets to the limiting image of the unit ball.
   329	
   330	  Put
   331	  \[
   332	    M=\|\mathcal{E}_\chi:H^\sigma(\mathbb{T}_L)\to H^\sigma(\R^d)\|
   333	    \|\mathcal{P}_\psi:H^{\sigma+\gamma}(\R^d)
   334	    \to H^{\sigma+\gamma}(\mathbb{T}_L)\|.
   335	  \]
   336	  The outer Bessel maps are unitary. For $j \ge 3^d$, choose $n = \lfloor
   337	  j^{1/d}/4\rfloor$. Then
   338	  \[
   339	    (2n+1)^d\le(j^{1/d}/2+1)^d<j,\qquad
   340	    \|K-K_n\|\le M(2L/\pi)^\gamma j^{-\gamma/d}.
   341	  \]
   342	  The second estimate follows from $n+1 > j^{1/d}/4$. For a compact operator,
   343	  every rank less than $j$ approximation $F$ satisfies $s_j(K) \le \|K-F\|$: the
   344	  span of the first $j$ right singular vectors contains a unit vector in $\ker
   345	  F$, on which $\|K\cdot\| \ge s_j(K)$. If $s_j(K) = 0$ the inequality is
   346	  immediate. For $j < 3^d$ use $s_j(K) \le \|K\| \le M$. Thus, one may take
   347	  \[
   348	    C_{\chi,\sigma,\gamma,d}
   349	    =M\max(3^\gamma,(2L/\pi)^\gamma).
   350	  \]
   351	  Finally, $\sum_j j^{-p\gamma/d}$ converges for $p\gamma > d$. This proves
   352	  Proposition~\ref{P:cutoff-singular-values}.
   353	\end{proof}
   354	
   355	No uniform support-radius constant or endpoint necessity is asserted in
   356	Proposition~\ref{P:cutoff-singular-values}. The periodic inclusion was only a
   357	factor of the recovered whole-space operator.

   359	\subsection{Balanced adjoints and localized variance envelopes}
   360	
   361	For $E = H^{1/2}(\R^d)\times H^{-1/2}(\R^d)$ use the physical unitary
   362	coordinates
   363	\[
   364	  J_0(u,v)=(\Lambda^{1/2}u,\Lambda^{-1/2}v),\qquad
   365	  H=L^2(\R^d;\mathbb{C}^2).
   366	\]
   367	The frequency map $J$ in Section~\ref{S:wave-variance} is
   368	$(\mathcal{F}\oplus\mathcal{F})J_0$. Let $D_\chi$ multiply both phase entries
   369	and define
   370	\begin{align}
   371	  P_\chi&=J_0D_\chi J_0^{-1},\qquad
   372	  D_\gamma=\operatorname{diag}(\Lambda^{-\gamma},\Lambda^{-\gamma}),
   373	  \label{E:compact-balanced-cutoff}\\
   374	  K_{\rm out}&=P_\chi D_\gamma,\qquad
   375	  K_{\rm in}=P_\chi^*D_\gamma.
   376	  \label{E:compact-two-factors}
   377	\end{align}
   378	
   379	\begin{proposition}[Both compact envelopes]\label{P:compact-two-envelopes}
   380	  The operator $P_\chi$ is bounded. For the unitary swap $U(v,w) = (w,v)$,
   381	  \[
   382	    P_\chi^*=UP_\chi U,\qquad K_{\rm in}=UK_{\rm out}U.
   383	  \]
   384	  Both factors are compact and have equal $S_p$ norms for $p \ge 1$, $p\gamma >
   385	  d$. For $p \ge 2$, $p\gamma > d$, the positive compact operators
   386	  \[
   387	    B_{\rm out}=P_\chi D_\gamma^2P_\chi^*=K_{\rm out}K_{\rm out}^*,
   388	    \qquad B_{\rm in}=P_\chi^*D_\gamma^2P_\chi=K_{\rm in}K_{\rm in}^*
   389	  \]
   390	  satisfy
   391	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-envelope-traces}
   392	    \operatorname{Tr}B_{\rm out}^{p/2}
   393	    =\operatorname{Tr}B_{\rm in}^{p/2}=\|K_{\rm out}\|_{S_p}^p.
   394	  \end{equation}
   395	\end{proposition}
   396	
   397	\begin{proof}
   398	  Put $A_\sigma = \Lambda^\sigma\chi\Lambda^{-\sigma}$. The full-Lebesgue Schur
   399	  argument in Lemma~\ref{L:cutoff-factorization} shows boundedness for every
   400	  real $\sigma$. On Schwartz functions, self-adjointness of real multiplication
   401	  and of the Bessel powers gives $A_\sigma^* = A_{-\sigma}$. Density and
   402	  boundedness extend this to the Hilbert adjoints. No evenness of $\chi$ is
   403	  needed. Thus,
   404	  \[
   405	    P_\chi=\operatorname{diag}(A_{1/2},A_{-1/2}),\qquad
   406	    P_\chi^*=\operatorname{diag}(A_{-1/2},A_{1/2})=UP_\chi U.
   407	  \]
   408	  The swap commutes with $D_\gamma$, giving the claimed factor identity. The
   409	  blocks of $K_{\rm out}$ are $K_{\chi,1/2,\gamma}$ and $K_{\chi,-1/2,\gamma}$.
   410	  Proposition~\ref{P:cutoff-singular-values} gives compactness and $S_p$
   411	  membership. The singular values of their direct sum form the multiset union,
   412	  so
   413	  \[
   414	    \|K_{\rm out}\|_{S_p}^p
   415	    =\|K_{\chi,1/2,\gamma}\|_{S_p}^p+
   416	    \|K_{\chi,-1/2,\gamma}\|_{S_p}^p.
   417	  \]
   418	  Unitary conjugation preserves them. Finally, the positive eigenvalues of
   419	  $KK^*$ and $K^*K$ agree with multiplicity: on an eigenspace with eigenvalue
   420	  $\lambda > 0$, the maps $K/\sqrt\lambda$ and $K^*/\sqrt\lambda$ are inverse
   421	  isometries. Zero eigenvalues contribute nothing to the trace. Summing these
   422	  scalar powers proves~\eqref{E:compact-envelope-traces}. This proves
   423	  Proposition~\ref{P:compact-two-envelopes}.
   424	\end{proof}
   425	
   426	We use the usual positive square root of a bounded positive operator and the
   427	spectral decomposition of compact positive operators. The needed order argument
   428	is recorded explicitly.
   429	
   430	\begin{lemma}[Compact positive order and trace]\label{L:compact-positive-order}
   431	  If $A,B$ are bounded self-adjoint operators with $0 \le A \le B$ and $B$
   432	  compact positive, then $A$ is compact and its ordered eigenvalues satisfy
   433	  $\lambda_j(A) \le \lambda_j(B)$, including zero padding. Consequently, for $t
   434	  \ge 1$ with finite $\operatorname{Tr}B^t$,
   435	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-positive-trace}
   436	    \operatorname{Tr}A^t\le\operatorname{Tr}B^t.
   437	  \end{equation}
   438	\end{lemma}
   439	
   440	\begin{proof}
   441	  Let $Q_n$ be finite spectral projections of $B$ whose tails tend to zero in
   442	  norm. Then
   443	  \[
   444	    \|(1-Q_n)A^{1/2}\|^2
   445	    =\|(1-Q_n)A(1-Q_n)\|
   446	    \le\|(1-Q_n)B(1-Q_n)\|\longrightarrow0.
   447	  \]
   448	  Thus, $A^{1/2}$ is a norm limit of finite-rank operators and is compact, as is
   449	  $A$. For compact positive operators, the max-min formula for $\lambda_j$
   450	  follows in an eigenbasis: the span of the first $j$ eigenvectors gives the
   451	  lower bound for the supremum over $j$-dimensional subspaces of their minimum
   452	  Rayleigh quotient, while every such subspace meets the orthogonal complement
   453	  of the first $j-1$ eigenvectors, giving the upper bound. Compare the Rayleigh
   454	  quotients of $A$ and $B$ to obtain the eigenvalue inequality. Sum the ordered
   455	  scalar powers to prove \eqref{E:compact-positive-trace}. No inequality $A^t
   456	  \le B^t$ is asserted. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:compact-positive-order}.
   457	\end{proof}
   458	
   459	\begin{proposition}[Localized finite variance bounds]\label{P:localized-finite-variance}
   460	  Suppose finitely many bounded operators $Z_\ell$ on $H$ satisfy
   461	  \begin{equation}\label{E:localized-finite-hypotheses}
   462	    P_\chi Z_\ell=Z_\ell=Z_\ell P_\chi,\qquad
   463	    V_{\rm out}:=\sum_\ell Z_\ell Z_\ell^*\le CD_\gamma^2,\qquad
   464	    V_{\rm in}:=\sum_\ell Z_\ell^*Z_\ell\le CD_\gamma^2,
   465	  \end{equation}
   466	  with $C \ge 0$. If $p \ge 2$ and $p\gamma > d$, every $Z_\ell$ is compact in
   467	  $S_p$, the two variances are compact in $S_{p/2}$, and
   468	  \begin{align}
   469	    V_{\rm out}&\le CB_{\rm out},\qquad V_{\rm in}\le CB_{\rm in},
   470	    \label{E:localized-two-envelopes}\\
   471	    \operatorname{Tr}V_{\rm out}^{p/2},\quad
   472	    \operatorname{Tr}V_{\rm in}^{p/2}
   473	    &\le C^{p/2}\|K_{\rm out}\|_{S_p}^p.
   474	    \label{E:localized-trace-bounds}
   475	  \end{align}
   476	\end{proposition}
   477	
   478	\begin{proof}
   479	  Left localization gives $V_{\rm out} = P_\chi V_{\rm out}P_\chi^*$. Apply
   480	  positive congruence to the output bound
   481	  in~\eqref{E:localized-finite-hypotheses} to get $V_{\rm out} \le CP_\chi
   482	  D_\gamma^2P_\chi^* = CB_{\rm out}$. Right localization similarly gives $V_{\rm
   483	  in} = P_\chi^*V_{\rm in}P_\chi \le CB_{\rm in}$.
   484	  Proposition~\ref{P:compact-two-envelopes} and
   485	  Lemma~\ref{L:compact-positive-order} prove compactness and the two trace
   486	  bounds with $t = p/2$. If $C = 0$, both variances and every $Z_\ell$ vanish,
   487	  so all assertions are immediate.
   488	
   489	  For each $\ell$, $Z_\ell Z_\ell^* \le V_{\rm out}$ is compact by the same
   490	  lemma. Its finite spectral projections $Q_n$ give $\|(1-Q_n)Z_\ell\|^2 =
   491	  \|(1-Q_n)Z_\ell Z_\ell^*(1-Q_n)\| \to 0$. Hence, $Z_\ell$ is compact. Its
   492	  singular values squared are the nonzero eigenvalues of $Z_\ell Z_\ell^*$.
   493	  Comparing with $V_{\rm out}$ and summing proves $Z_\ell \in S_p$ with
   494	  $\|Z_\ell\|_{S_p}^p \le \operatorname{Tr}V_{\rm out}^{p/2}$. This proves
   495	  Proposition~\ref{P:localized-finite-variance}.
   496	\end{proof}
   497	
   498	The two localization identities are hypotheses here; a noise coefficient family
   499	has not yet been shown to satisfy them. In particular, $P_\chi$ is not assumed
   500	self-adjoint or a projection.
   501	
   502	\begin{corollary}[Finite Gaussian operators]\label{C:finite-gaussian-operators}
   503	  Under~\eqref{E:localized-finite-hypotheses}, let $g_\ell$ be independent real
   504	  standard Gaussians. For even $p \ge 2$ with $p\gamma > d$, the finite sum $X =
   505	  \sum_\ell g_\ell Z_\ell$ satisfies
   506	  \begin{equation}\label{E:finite-gaussian-operator-bound}
   507	    (\E\|X\|_{S_p}^p)^{1/p}
   508	    \le\sqrt{p-1}\sqrt C\|K_{\rm out}\|_{S_p}.
   509	  \end{equation}
   510	  Its extended norm is measurable, with finite expectation as displayed.
   511	\end{corollary}
   512	
   513	\begin{proof}
   514	  Choose finite-rank orthogonal projections $\Pi_n$ from a countable orthonormal
   515	  basis of $H$, with $\Pi_n \to I$ strongly. Put $Z_{\ell,n} = \Pi_nZ_\ell\Pi_n$
   516	  and $X_n = \sum_\ell g_\ell Z_{\ell,n}$, viewed as matrices on
   517	  $\operatorname{ran}\Pi_n$. Their output variance satisfies
   518	  \[
   519	    \sum_\ell\Pi_nZ_\ell\Pi_nZ_\ell^*\Pi_n
   520	    \le\Pi_nV_{\rm out}\Pi_n,
   521	  \]
   522	  since the difference is $\sum_\ell\Pi_nZ_\ell(1-\Pi_n)Z_\ell^*\Pi_n \ge 0$.
   523	  The input inequality is identical with adjoints interchanged. Compact max-min
   524	  also gives $\lambda_j(\Pi_nV\Pi_n) \le \lambda_j(V)$ for positive compact $V$,
   525	  since Rayleigh subspaces inside $\operatorname{ran}\Pi_n$ form a subset of all
   526	  subspaces. Thus, both variance trace powers of these matrices are bounded by
   527	  $C^{p/2}\|K_{\rm out}\|_{S_p}^p$.
   528	
   529	  Proposition~\ref{P:finite-gaussian-matrix} applies to these finite complex
   530	  matrices, the same real independent Gaussians and the even $p$. Taking the
   531	  average of the two already bounded trace powers gives
   532	  \begin{equation}\label{E:finite-gaussian-compression-bound}
   533	    \E\|X_n\|_{S_p}^p
   534	    \le(p-1)^{p/2}C^{p/2}\|K_{\rm out}\|_{S_p}^p.
   535	  \end{equation}
   536	  No factor two is added by this average.
   537	
   538	  For each Gaussian coordinate vector, $X$ is a finite sum of compact operators.
   539	  Strong convergence of $\Pi_n$ implies $\Pi_nX\Pi_n \to X$ in operator norm:
   540	  approximate $X$ by a finite-rank $F$, use uniform strong convergence on the
   541	  finite-dimensional ranges of $F$ and $F^*$, and control the remainder using
   542	  $\|\Pi_n\| \le 1$. Singular values are norm-Lipschitz. Indeed, their formula
   543	  \[
   544	    s_j(A)=\inf_{\dim L<j}
   545	    \sup_{v\in L^\perp,\ \|v\|=1}\|Av\|
   546	  \]
   547	  follows from compact singular vectors and gives $s_j(A) \le s_j(B)+\|A-B\|$,
   548	  and the reverse bound by interchanging $A,B$. Hence, $s_j(X_n) \to s_j(X)$ for
   549	  each $j$. Fatou for the nonnegative singular-value sum gives $\|X\|_{S_p}^p
   550	  \le \liminf_n\|X_n\|_{S_p}^p$, allowing extended infinity. These variables are
   551	  measurable: the finite Gaussian coordinate map into operators is
   552	  norm-continuous, each singular value is continuous, and the norm power is
   553	  their nonnegative measurable sum. Fatou in probability
   554	  and~\eqref{E:finite-gaussian-compression-bound} prove the bound and
   555	  almost-sure finiteness. No $S_p$-Bochner convergence is assumed. This proves
   556	  Corollary~\ref{C:finite-gaussian-operators}.
   557	\end{proof}
