   167	\subsection{Forms on the full phase}
   168	
   169	Choose and fix $T > 0$. Set $\Lambda = (1-\Delta)^{1/2}$, $s = 1/2$ and $E_r =
   170	H^r(\R^d)\times H^{r-1}(\R^d)$. On the complexification of $E = E_s$, use inner
   171	products linear in the first slot. The map
   172	\[
   173	  Jz(\xi) = \left(\langle\xi\rangle^{1/2}\widehat{z}_1(\xi),
   174	  \langle\xi\rangle^{-1/2}\widehat{z}_2(\xi)\right)
   175	\]
   176	is unitary onto $L^2(\R^d;\mathbb{C}^2)$. The full massless wave group has
   177	Fourier matrix
   178	\begin{equation}\label{E:variance-free-matrix}
   179	  S(t,\xi) =
   180	  \begin{pmatrix}
   181	    \cos(t|\xi|) & \sin(t|\xi|)/|\xi|\\
   182	    -|\xi|\sin(t|\xi|) & \cos(t|\xi|)
   183	  \end{pmatrix},
   184	\end{equation}
   185	where the sine quotient is $t$ at zero. Let $B(b)(u,v) = (0,bu)$. Choose and fix
   186	a real even nonnegative $\zeta \in C_c^\infty(\R^d)$ equal to one on $B_1$ and
   187	zero off $B_2$, and put $\zeta_R(x) = \zeta(x/R)$ for $R > 0$. For $I =
   188	[t_0,t_0+h] \subset [0,T]$, $0 < h \le 1$, and Schwartz phases $z,w$, put
   189	\begin{align}
   190	  v_z(t) &= [S(t)z]_1,
   191	  \label{E:variance-displacement}\\
   192	  G_w(t) &= -\frac{\sin(t|D|)}{|D|}\Lambda w_1
   193	  +\cos(t|D|)\Lambda^{-1}w_2,
   194	  \label{E:variance-dual-wave}\\
   195	  F_{z,w}(t,x) &= 1_I(t)v_z(t,x)\overline{G_w(t,x)},
   196	  \qquad \ell_R(I;z,w) = W_{\mathbb{C}}(\zeta_RF_{z,w}),
   197	  \label{E:variance-actual-form}
   198	\end{align}
   199	where $W_{\mathbb{C}}(F) = W(\operatorname{Re}F)+iW(\operatorname{Im}F)$. There
   200	is no observation cutoff in this definition.
   201	
   202	We first assume $\Gamma \ne 0$. If $\Gamma = 0$, all forms and the column maps
   203	below are zero, so their bounds hold directly. For the nonzero case, let $\nu_R$
   204	be~\eqref{E:masked-auxiliary-measure} and set
   205	\begin{equation}\label{E:variance-actual-growth-constant}
   206	  L_\zeta = \|\widehat{\zeta}\|_1,\qquad
   207	  C_\nu = c_d^2L_\zeta^2C_\Gamma.
   208	\end{equation}
   209	Proposition~\ref{P:masked-auxiliary-norm} gives a positive even tempered Radon
   210	measure with $\nu_R(B(y,r)) \le C_\nu r^\alpha$, uniformly in $R$.
   211	
   212	\begin{proposition}[Form and phase kernel]\label{P:actual-wave-form}
   213	  The tests $\zeta_RF_{z,w}$ in~\eqref{E:variance-actual-form} belong to the
   214	  original noise completion. The form $\ell_R$ is linear in $z$ and conjugate
   215	  linear in $w$, and uses the same $W$ as the model. For a smooth deterministic
   216	  coefficient $b$ with common compact spatial support and bounded spatial
   217	  derivatives on $[0,T]$,
   218	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-physical-adjoint}
   219	    \langle S(-t)B(b(t))S(t)z,w\rangle_E
   220	    = \int b(t,x)v_z(t,x)\overline{G_w(t,x)}\ud x.
   221	  \end{equation}
   222	  For a real compact smooth $\chi$, multiplication $D_\chi$ on both phase
   223	  entries has adjoint
   224	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-cutoff-adjoint}
   225	    D_\chi^{*,E}w
   226	    = \left(\Lambda^{-1}\chi\Lambda w_1,
   227	    \Lambda\chi\Lambda^{-1}w_2\right).
   228	  \end{equation}
   229	  With $U = Jz$, $V = Jw$, $r = |\xi|$, $\rho = |\eta|$ and the continuous
   230	  functions $c_r,b_r$ of Lemma~\ref{L:masked-continuous-wave}, set
   231	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-normalized-kernel}
   232	    \mathcal{K}(t;\xi,\eta)
   233	    = \frac1{\sqrt{\langle\xi\rangle\langle\eta\rangle}}
   234	    \begin{pmatrix}
   235	      -b_rc_\rho & -b_rb_\rho\\
   236	      c_rc_\rho & c_rb_\rho
   237	    \end{pmatrix}(t).
   238	  \end{equation}
   239	  Then
   240	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-normalized-covariance}
   241	    \E|\ell_R(I;z,w)|^2
   242	    \le \int\left\|\int\sum_{i,j=1}^2
   243	    1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\eta+\lambda,\eta)
   244	    U_j(\eta)\overline{V_i(\eta+\lambda)}\ud\eta
   245	    \right\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\nu_R(\ud\lambda).
   246	  \end{equation}
   247	\end{proposition}
   248	
   249	\begin{proof}
   250	  The wave multipliers are smooth at zero through the continuous sine quotient,
   251	  with polynomially bounded frequency derivatives on finite time intervals.
   252	  Bessel multipliers preserve Schwartz space. Thus, $v_z,G_w$ and their product
   253	  are continuous in all Schwartz seminorms on $[0,T]$. For tests supported in a
   254	  fixed compact $K$, the absolute spatial pairing is bounded by
   255	  \[
   256	    |K|\Gamma(K-K)\|F(t)\|_\infty\|H(u)\|_\infty.
   257	  \]
   258	  Indeed, only $y \in K-K$ contributes to $\int\Gamma(\ud y)\int
   259	  F(t,x)\overline{H(u,x-y)}\ud x$. Combine this with the temporal Schur bound
   260	  and approximate the interval indicator and the continuous time dependence by
   261	  smooth interior temporal tests, keeping the spatial support of $\zeta_R$. This
   262	  admits the masked product in the original completion in every allowed
   263	  dimension.
   264	
   265	  We also identify its auxiliary and spectral limits. Approximate a
   266	  Schwartz-valued function on $I$ by time partitions with frozen spatial values,
   267	  and then replace the finitely many indicators by compact smooth temporal
   268	  functions. A diagonal sequence $F_n$ of finite temporal tensors converges in
   269	  $L^2$ time in every Schwartz seminorm. Fourier integration by parts and the
   270	  spatial weighted supremum bounds give, for sufficiently large fixed $N$,

271	  \[
   272	    \|\widehat{F_n-F}(\xi)\|_{L^2(0,T)}
   273	    \le \epsilon_n\langle\xi\rangle^{-N},\qquad \epsilon_n \to 0.
   274	  \]
   275	  Choose $N$ so that the square weight is integrable against both tempered
   276	  measures $\mu$ and $\nu_R$. Lemma~\ref{L:masked-time-completion} gives
   277	  convergence in their spectral $H_a$ norms. Multiplication by the fixed
   278	  $\zeta_R$ preserves these $L^2$ Schwartz-seminorm limits, so the masked
   279	  differences converge in the $\mu$ spectral norm too. The preceding
   280	  compact-support estimate also gives convergence in the original completion.
   281	  Hence, the auxiliary extension and original-noise limit agree on these
   282	  products. Constants for this admission argument may depend on $R$; they are
   283	  not the uniform variance constants below.
   284	
   285	  For real tensor tests $f,g$, the Hermitian symmetry of their spatial
   286	  transforms gives
   287	  \[
   288	    A(-\xi) = \overline{A(\xi)},\qquad
   289	    A(\xi) = \langle\widehat{f}(\xi),\widehat{g}(\xi)\rangle_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}.
   290	  \]
   291	  Integration against either even $\mu$ or even $\nu_R$ cancels the imaginary
   292	  mixed term. Expanding the squared norm of $\widehat{f}+i\widehat{g}$, then
   293	  using the preceding approximation, extends
   294	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-noise-completion} to the present complex tests:
   295	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-complex-noise}
   296	    \E|W_{\mathbb{C}}(\zeta_RF)|^2
   297	    = (2\pi)^d\int\|\widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\mu(\ud\xi)
   298	    \le (2\pi)^d\int\|\widehat{F}(\lambda)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\nu_R(\ud\lambda).
   299	  \end{equation}
   300	  This is a bound for the masked noise, not a declaration that its law is
   301	  stationary. Complex linearity of $W_{\mathbb{C}}$ and linearity of $v_z,G_w$
   302	  prove the stated sesquilinearity.
   303	
   304	  Smooth multiplication is bounded on each Sobolev space: Fourier convolution,
   305	  the inequality $\langle\xi\rangle^r\langle\eta\rangle^{-r} \le
   306	  2^{|r|/2}\langle\xi-\eta\rangle^{|r|}$ and weighted Schwartz decay reduce this
   307	  to the $L^1*L^2$ bound. The free matrix is strongly continuous and bounded on
   308	  $E$ on compact time intervals, directly by its weighted Fourier entries. Thus,
   309	  the ordinary first-response integral exists on states. Since $S(-t)(0,f) =
   310	  (-\sin(t|D|)f/|D|,\cos(t|D|)f)$, moving the real self-adjoint multipliers and
   311	  the two Sobolev weights onto $w$ proves \eqref{E:variance-physical-adjoint}.
   312	  The same weighted duality gives \eqref{E:variance-cutoff-adjoint}. Inserting
   313	  this adjoint in $G_w$ is the correctly observed form; $D_\chi$ need not be
   314	  self-adjoint on $E$. This deterministic identity does not identify a
   315	  positive-width source with the original noise or assert a source limit.
   316	
   317	  The definitions give exactly
   318	  \begin{align*}
   319	    \widehat{v}_z(t,\eta)
   320	    &= \langle\eta\rangle^{-1/2}
   321	    [c_\rho(t)U_1(\eta)+b_\rho(t)U_2(\eta)],\\
   322	    \widehat{G}_w(t,\xi)
   323	    &= \langle\xi\rangle^{-1/2}
   324	    [-b_r(t)V_1(\xi)+c_r(t)V_2(\xi)].
   325	  \end{align*}
   326	  Their product gives~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-kernel}. At zero frequencies
   327	  one uses the continuous sine quotient, not division by zero; at $\xi = \eta =
   328	  0$ the matrix is
   329	  $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}-t&-t^2\\1&t\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Fourier
   330	  multiplication with the conjugate yields
   331	  \[
   332	    \widehat{F}_{z,w}(t,-\lambda)
   333	    = c_d1_I(t)\int\sum_{i,j=1}^2\mathcal{K}_{ij}(t;\eta+\lambda,\eta)
   334	    U_j(\eta)\overline{V_i(\eta+\lambda)}\ud\eta.
   335	  \]
   336	  The spatial integral is absolutely convergent uniformly on the finite time
   337	  interval by Schwartz decay. The Schur bound also makes it a Bochner
   338	  $H_a^{\mathbb{C}}$ integral. Reflect $\lambda$ using evenness of $\nu_R$
   339	  in~\eqref{E:variance-complex-noise}. Since $(2\pi)^dc_d^2 = 1$, this
   340	  proves~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-covariance} with no remaining Fourier
   341	  factor. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:actual-wave-form}.
   342	\end{proof}

   344	\subsection{Bessel's inequality and the two variances}
   345	
   346	\begin{lemma}[Hilbert-valued finite Bessel inequality]\label{L:phase-bessel}
   347	  Let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, let $\{u_k\}$ be a finite
   348	  orthonormal family in $L^2(\R^d;\mathbb{C}^2)$, and let $g = (g_1,g_2) \in
   349	  L^2(\R^d;H^2)$. Then
   350	  \begin{equation}\label{E:phase-bessel}
   351	    \sum_k\left\|\int\sum_{j=1}^2u_{k,j}(\eta)g_j(\eta)\ud\eta\right\|_H^2
   352	    \le \int\sum_{j=1}^2\|g_j(\eta)\|_H^2\ud\eta.
   353	  \end{equation}
   354	  The same bound holds with $\overline{u_{k,j}}$ in place of $u_{k,j}$.
   355	\end{lemma}
   356	
   357	\begin{proof}
   358	  Expand $g$ in a countable orthonormal basis of $H$. On each scalar coefficient
   359	  apply scalar Bessel to the orthonormal family $\{\overline{u_k}\}$, or to
   360	  $\{u_k\}$ for the conjugated version. Scalar finite Bessel follows by
   361	  subtracting an orthogonal finite projection and expanding its nonnegative
   362	  squared norm. Sum over the $H$ basis and use Parseval and nonnegative Tonelli.
   363	  The Bochner integrals exist by $L^2$ Cauchy--Schwarz. A finite-dimensional $H$
   364	  uses its finite basis, and the zero space is immediate. No independence is
   365	  involved. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:phase-bessel}.
   366	\end{proof}
   367	
   368	\begin{proposition}[Both variance directions]\label{P:wave-two-variances}
   369	  There is a finite $C_T$, depending on the fixed model, mask,
   370	  $a,\alpha,\gamma,T$, but not on $R,I$ or the orthonormal family, such that for
   371	  every finite complex $E$-orthonormal Schwartz family $\{e_k\}$ and every
   372	  Schwartz phase $z$,
   373	  \begin{align}
   374	    \sum_k\E|\ell_R(I;e_k,z)|^2
   375	    &\le C_T h^{2-a}B_\alpha(h)\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2,
   376	    \label{E:wave-input-variance}\\
   377	    \sum_k\E|\ell_R(I;z,e_k)|^2
   378	    &\le C_T h^{2-a}B_\alpha(h)\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2.
   379	    \label{E:wave-output-variance}
   380	  \end{align}
   381	  For every $\beta$ in~\eqref{E:variance-beta-range}, either right side may be
   382	  replaced by $C_{T,\beta}h^{2\beta}\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2$.
   383	\end{proposition}
   384	
   385	\begin{proof}
   386	  Each entry in~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-kernel} is a product of two
   387	  continuous wave factors times $(\langle\xi\rangle\langle\eta\rangle)^{-1/2}$,
   388	  with a possible minus sign. Lemma~\ref{L:masked-continuous-wave} therefore
   389	  gives
   390	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-kernel-time-bound}
   391	    \|1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\xi,\eta)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2
   392	    \le A_T h^{2-a}\Phi_h(\xi,\eta),
   393	    \qquad A_T = C_1(a)(1+T)^4.
   394	  \end{equation}
   395	  The positive even Radon measure $\nu_R$ satisfies the growth bound
   396	  \eqref{E:variance-actual-growth-constant}. Thus, all hypotheses of
   397	  Proposition~\ref{P:frequency-row} hold, and
   398	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-actual-row-bound}
   399	    \int\Phi_h(\xi,\xi-\lambda)\nu_R(\ud\lambda)
   400	    \le K C_\nu B_\alpha(h)\langle\xi\rangle^{-2\gamma}.
   401	  \end{equation}
   402	  No nonnegative physical inverse covariance of $\nu_R$ is needed.
   403	
   404	  The kernels used in Lemma~\ref{L:phase-bessel} belong to its stated $L^2$
   405	  space for each fixed $\lambda$. Indeed, $|c_r(t)| \le 1$ and $|b_r(t)| \le
   406	  \sqrt{2}\max(1,T)$ on $[0,T]$, by the high- and low-frequency representations.
   407	  The kernels are continuous into $L^2(0,T)$ in their frequency variables, hence
   408	  into $H_a^{\mathbb{C}}$ by Schur. Separability gives strong measurability.
   409	  Multiplication by shifted Schwartz components of $U$ or $V$ then gives the
   410	  required $L^2$ integrability. Later $\lambda$ integrals are of nonnegative
   411	  functions; their finiteness follows from the estimates below.
   412	
   413	  First fix $V = Jz$ and let $U_k = Je_k$ be the input family.
   414	  In~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-covariance} set
   415	  \[
   416	    g_j^\lambda(\eta) = \sum_{i=1}^2
   417	    1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\eta+\lambda,\eta)
   418	    \overline{V_i(\eta+\lambda)}.
   419	  \]
   420	  Lemma~\ref{L:phase-bessel} and Cauchy--Schwarz over the two output components
   421	  give
   422	  \begin{align*}
   423	    \sum_j\|g_j^\lambda(\eta)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2
   424	    &\le 2\sum_{i,j}|V_i(\eta+\lambda)|^2
   425	    \|1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\eta+\lambda,\eta)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\\
   426	    &\le 4A_T h^{2-a}\Phi_h(\eta+\lambda,\eta)
   427	    \sum_i|V_i(\eta+\lambda)|^2.
   428	  \end{align*}
   429	  Change variables $\xi = \eta+\lambda$ in the Lebesgue integral for each
   430	  $\lambda$, apply Tonelli and~\eqref{E:variance-actual-row-bound}, and use
   431	  $\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}} = \|\langle\xi\rangle^{-\gamma}Jz\|_2$. This
   432	  proves~\eqref{E:wave-input-variance} with $C_T = 4A_TKC_\nu$.
   433	
   434	  Next fix $U = Jz$ and let $V_k = Je_k$ be the output family. After $\eta =
   435	  \xi-\lambda$ in~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-covariance}, put
   436	  \[
   437	    f_i^\lambda(\xi) = \sum_{j=1}^2
   438	    1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\xi,\xi-\lambda)U_j(\xi-\lambda).
   439	  \]
   440	  Apply the conjugated version of Lemma~\ref{L:phase-bessel}. Cauchy--Schwarz
   441	  over the two input components bounds its right side by
   442	  \[
   443	    4A_T h^{2-a}\int\Phi_h(\xi,\xi-\lambda)
   444	    \sum_j|U_j(\xi-\lambda)|^2\ud\xi.
   445	  \]
   446	  After the change of variables and Tonelli, the row at fixed $\eta$ is
   447	  $\int\Phi_h(\eta+\lambda,\eta)\nu_R(\ud\lambda)$. Reflect $\lambda$ using the
   448	  evenness of $\nu_R$ and then use symmetry of $\Phi_h$. This row becomes
   449	  $\int\Phi_h(\eta,\eta-\lambda)\nu_R(\ud\lambda)$, which is bounded
   450	  by~\eqref{E:variance-actual-row-bound} with $\xi = \eta$. This proves
   451	  \eqref{E:wave-output-variance} with the same $C_T$.
   452	
   453	  Use Corollary~\ref{C:frequency-time} for $h^{2-a}$ times the row integral at
   454	  the two applications above to obtain the asserted $h^{2\beta}$ bounds,
   455	  including strict absorption of the critical logarithm. The constants are
   456	  uniform in $R,I$ and family size. The $R$-dependent admission estimate was not
   457	  used as this uniform variance bound. This proves
   458	  Proposition~\ref{P:wave-two-variances}.
   459	\end{proof}

   461	\subsection{Mean-square columns on the original probability space}
   462	
   463	Write $E_r^{\mathrm{real}}$ for the real phase space in dimension $d$.
   464	
   465	\begin{proposition}[Column and adjoint-column maps]\label{P:wave-square-columns}
   466	  On the same probability space there are deterministic bounded real linear maps
   467	  \[
   468	    m_{R,I},n_{R,I}:E_{s-\gamma}^{\mathrm{real}}\longrightarrow
   469	    L^2(\Omega;E_s^{\mathrm{real}}),
   470	  \]
   471	  with squared bounds $C_T h^{2-a}B_\alpha(h)$, such that, for every fixed real
   472	  Schwartz pair $z,w$,
   473	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-square-columns}
   474	    \langle m_{R,I}z,w\rangle_E
   475	    = \ell_R(I;z,w) = \langle z,n_{R,I}w\rangle_E
   476	    \quad\text{in }L^2(\Omega).
   477	  \end{equation}
   478	  Fixed-vector values and finite families of values are centered Gaussian.
   479	\end{proposition}
   480	
   481	\begin{proof}
   482	  Choose a countable real Schwartz orthonormal basis $\{e_k\}$ of $E_s$. Such a
   483	  basis follows by Gram--Schmidt from a countable dense Schwartz family,
   484	  discarding zero residuals. Schwartz density follows by smooth Fourier cutoff
   485	  approximation in the weighted $L^2$ norms: approximate by compact smooth
   486	  Fourier coordinates, replace $g(\xi)$ by $(g(\xi)+\overline{g(-\xi)})/2$, and
   487	  apply the inverse Bessel/Fourier maps. The resulting phases are real Schwartz,
   488	  and Gram--Schmidt preserves that class. The same density holds in
   489	  $E_{s-\gamma}$.
   490	
   491	  For fixed real Schwartz $z$, define
   492	  \[
   493	    m_N(z) = \sum_{k\le N}\ell_R(I;z,e_k)e_k,
   494	    \qquad n_N(z) = \sum_{k\le N}\ell_R(I;e_k,z)e_k.
   495	  \]
   496	  Both are finite Gaussian sums on the original $W$. By
   497	  Proposition~\ref{P:wave-two-variances}, their coefficient expected squares
   498	  have finite sum. Orthogonality gives the squared tail norms as the
   499	  corresponding sums of expected squares. Thus, both sequences converge in
   500	  $L^2(\Omega;E_s)$ to $m(z),n(z)$ with the asserted bounds, without
   501	  independence of the coefficients. Finite-sum measurability and separable $E_s$
   502	  give strong measurability of the limits. The bounded real linear maps extend
   503	  uniquely from Schwartz phases to $E_{s-\gamma}$.
   504	
   505	  If $w_N$ is the $E_s$ projection of a Schwartz $w$ onto the first $N$ basis
   506	  vectors, then $\langle m_N(z),w\rangle_E = \ell_R(I;z,w_N)$. The singleton
   507	  form of~\eqref{E:wave-output-variance}, after normalizing $w-w_N$ in $E_s$,
   508	  gives
   509	  \[
   510	    \E|\ell_R(I;z,w-w_N)|^2
   511	    \le C_T h^{2-a}B_\alpha(h)\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2\|w-w_N\|_{E_s}^2.
   512	  \]
   513	  The zero residual is immediate. The right side tends to zero, giving the first
   514	  identity in~\eqref{E:variance-square-columns}. For the second, project $z$
   515	  instead and use the singleton input bound \eqref{E:wave-input-variance}. A
   516	  fixed countable Schwartz orthonormal basis and Parseval show basis
   517	  independence of the constructed limits.
   518	
   519	  Continuous linear functionals of the limits, and finite linear combinations of
   520	  such functionals, are $L^2$ limits of centered Gaussian variables with
   521	  convergent variances. Their characteristic functions therefore converge to
   522	  those of centered Gaussians. The same reasoning after the bounded input
   523	  extension proves joint Gaussianity for arbitrary fixed inputs and finite
   524	  families of the two maps. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:wave-square-columns}.
   525	\end{proof}
   526	
   527	These are maps into $L^2(\Omega;E_s)$ for fixed intervals. No common uncountable
   528	almost-sure version, random bounded operator, Hilbert--Schmidt realization, time
   529	path, source convergence or new solution-moment bound is inferred by this
   530	section alone. Both variance directions are retained in
   531	Section~\ref{S:actual-operator-driver}.
     1	\section{Spatial white noise: energy and explicit moment bounds}
     2	\label{S:intrinsic-white-evaluation}
     3	
     4	Take $d = \alpha = 1$ and $\Gamma = c\delta_0$, $c \ge 0$, with temporal kernel
     5	$|s-t|^{-a}$, $0 < a < 1$, and data $(1,0)$. The parameter $c$ is covariance
     6	mass; the coefficient of unit noise would be $\sqrt c$. No additional temporal
     7	normalization is inserted. The wave kinetic coefficient is one. For real unit $f
     8	\in H^1(\R)$ put $A = \int_\R f^4$ and $b = \int_\R(f')^2$. The physical
     9	covariance is $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f) = cA$.
    10	
    11	\begin{lemma}[A square identity for the distribution function]\label{L:white-cdf-square}
    12	  Every such $f$ has $A < \infty$. With $\mathsf{F}(x) =
    13	  \int_{-\infty}^xf(y)^2\ud y$, for every real $z$,
    14	  \begin{equation}\label{E:white-cdf-square}
    15	    0\le\int_\R[f'-zf(1-2\mathsf{F})]^2
    16	    =b-2zA+z^2/3 .
    17	  \end{equation}
    18	\end{lemma}
    19	
    20	\begin{proof}
    21	  On a bounded interval the weak derivative $f'$ is $L^1$ by Cauchy--Schwarz.
    22	  Its integral primitive has weak derivative $f'$ by Fubini. Subtracting it from
    23	  $f$ gives a function of weak derivative zero, hence constant almost
    24	  everywhere: test against derivatives of compact smooth primitives of all
    25	  zero-integral test functions. The resulting locally absolutely continuous
    26	  representatives patch on overlaps, giving one continuous representative. Thus,
    27	  $\rho = f^2$ is locally absolutely continuous with $\rho' = 2ff' \in L^1(\R)$,
    28	  while $\rho \ge 0$ and $\int\rho = 1$. Integrability of $\rho'$ makes $\rho$
    29	  Cauchy on each infinite tail, so it has finite limits at both ends. Its $L^1$
    30	  integrability forces both limits to be zero. It is therefore bounded, and $A =
    31	  \int\rho^2 \le \|\rho\|_\infty\int\rho < \infty$.
    32	
    33	  Now $0 \le \mathsf{F} \le 1$, $\mathsf{F}' = \rho$ continuously, and its
    34	  limits are zero and one. The derivative of $\rho(1-2\mathsf{F})$ is
    35	  $\rho'(1-2\mathsf{F})-2\rho^2 \in L^1$. Its endpoint limits vanish.
    36	  Integrating on $[-R,R]$ and sending $R \to \infty$ gives
    37	  \[
    38	    \int_\R f'f(1-2\mathsf{F})=A .
    39	  \]
    40	  The polynomial $P(y) = y-2y^2+(4/3)y^3$ has derivative $(1-2y)^2$. The chain
    41	  rule and the endpoints of $\mathsf{F}$ give
    42	  \[
    43	    \int_\R f^2(1-2\mathsf{F})^2=P(1)-P(0)=1/3 .
    44	  \]
    45	  Absolute integrability holds since this integrand is bounded by $f^2$. For
    46	  each real $z$, both terms in the square in~\eqref{E:white-cdf-square} are in
    47	  $L^2$, and their cross product is absolutely integrable. Expansion and the two
    48	  preceding identities prove the formula. Neither positivity of $f$ nor strict
    49	  increase of its CDF is required. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:white-cdf-square}.
    50	\end{proof}
    51	
    52	\begin{proposition}[Exact white spatial energy]\label{P:white-spatial-energy}
    53	  For $c > 0$,
    54	  \[
    55	    R_{\mathrm{sp}}=c/\sqrt3,\qquad
    56	    \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}=c^2/6.
    57	  \]
    58	  Both values are zero at $c = 0$.
    59	\end{proposition}
    60	
    61	\begin{proof}
    62	  Substitution $z = 3A$ into~\eqref{E:white-cdf-square} gives $3A^2 \le b$. This
    63	  is the exact premise and conclusion of the existing conditional WhiteCDF
    64	  square deduction. Here $A > 0$, since $A = 0$ would imply $f = 0$ a.e. Also $b
    65	  > 0$: zero derivative makes its continuous representative constant and hence
    66	  zero in $L^2$, contradicting unit mass. Thus, $A/\sqrt b \le 1/\sqrt3$.
    67	
    68	  For $\ell > 0$ use the real smooth $H^1$ profile $f_\ell(x) =
    69	  \sqrt{\ell/2}\operatorname{sech}(\ell x)$, with $f_\ell' = -\ell\tanh(\ell
    70	  x)f_\ell$. Set $t = \tanh(\ell x)$, so $\ud t = \ell\operatorname{sech}^2(\ell
    71	  x)\ud x$. Direct integration gives
    72	  \[
    73	    \int f_\ell^2=\frac12\int_{-1}^1\ud t=1,\quad
    74	    \int f_\ell^4=\frac\ell4\int_{-1}^1(1-t^2)\ud t=\ell/3,\quad
    75	    \int(f_\ell')^2=\frac{\ell^2}2\int_{-1}^1t^2\ud t=\ell^2/3.
    76	  \]
    77	  The ratio is attained, proving $R_{\mathrm{sp}} = c/\sqrt3$. The physical
    78	  Dirac measure introduces no Fourier constant or nonintegrable kernel
    79	  $|x|^{-1}$. The existing conditional energy deduction applies to $3A^2 \le b$:
    80	  \[
    81	    cA-b/2\le cA-\tfrac32A^2
    82	    =c^2/6-\tfrac32(A-c/3)^2\le c^2/6 .
    83	  \]
    84	  At $\ell = c > 0$ the profile attains $c^2/6$. These are full $H^1$ energy
    85	  profiles; compact approximation equality is
    86	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}, not a claim that the noncompact
    87	  profile itself is a compact stochastic control. At $c = 0$ the ratio is zero
    88	  and the energy is $\sup(-b/2) = 0$, approached by $f_\ell$ as
    89	  $\ell\downarrow0$. No zero-scale profile is used as a unit vector. The CDF,
    90	  integral and attainment arguments remain analytic; the two finite conditional
    91	  deductions do not formalize them. This proves
    92	  Proposition~\ref{P:white-spatial-energy}.
    93	\end{proof}
    94	
    95	\begin{theorem}[Explicit white moment bounds]\label{T:white-moment-bounds}
    96	  For the same original point limit,
    97	  \begin{equation}\label{E:white-moment-bounds}
    98	    \frac23\sqrt{\frac{c}{M_a}}\le C_2(c,a)
    99	    \le\frac23\sqrt{cK_0(a)},\qquad
   100	    K_0(a)=\frac{2^a}{1-a},\quad
   101	    M_a=\frac{\Gamma_E((1+a)/2)}
   102	    {\Gamma_E(1+a)\Gamma_E((1-a)/2)} .
   103	  \end{equation}
   104	  Its time exponent is $(3-a)/2$. These are bounds, not a numerical evaluation
   105	  of the intrinsic supremum.
   106	\end{theorem}
   107	
   108	\begin{proof}
   109	  Here $q = 3,k = 2,m = 3/2$. Formula~\eqref{E:spatial-static-energy-score}
   110	  gives
   111	  \[
   112	    F_0(z)=2\left[\frac{(2z)^{1/2}}{8\,3^{3/2}}\right]^{1/2}.
   113	  \]
   114	  For $c > 0$, $\sqrt{2\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}} = c/\sqrt3$, hence
   115	  $F_0(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}) = \sqrt c/(3\sqrt2)$ and
   116	  $2^mF_0(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}) = (2/3)\sqrt c$. Substitution into
   117	  Corollary~\ref{C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket}
   118	  proves~\eqref{E:white-moment-bounds} in the original units. All Gamma factors
   119	  are positive finite for $0 < a < 1$. At $c = 0$, $u = 1$ and $C_2 = 0$ by
   120	  Theorem~\ref{T:intrinsic-second-moment}; both displayed bounds vanish. This
   121	  proves Theorem~\ref{T:white-moment-bounds}.
   122	\end{proof}
   123	
   124	\begin{corollary}[Uniform relative width of the bound formulas]
   125	  \label{C:white-relative-width}
   126	  For $c > 0$, the ratio of the upper and lower formulas is
   127	  \[
   128	    \sqrt{K_0(a)M_a}
   129	    \le\left[\frac{\sqrt\pi}{2\Gamma_E(5/4)^2}\right]^{1/2},
   130	  \]
   131	  with equality at $a = 1/2$.
   132	\end{corollary}
   133	
   134	\begin{proof}
   135	  Duplication and recurrence from Lemma~\ref{L:equilibrium-gamma-beta} give
   136	  \[
   137	    \Gamma_E(1+a)
   138	    =\frac{2^a\Gamma_E((1+a)/2)\Gamma_E(1+a/2)}{\sqrt\pi},
   139	    \qquad
   140	    (1-a)\Gamma_E((1-a)/2)=2\Gamma_E((3-a)/2).
   141	  \]
   142	  Therefore,
   143	  \[
   144	    K_0(a)M_a
   145	    =\frac{\sqrt\pi}{2\Gamma_E(1+a/2)\Gamma_E((3-a)/2)} .
   146	  \]
   147	  Put $x = 1+a/2$, $y = (3-a)/2$, so $x,y > 0$ and $x+y = 5/2$. In Euler's Gamma
   148	  integral the $L^2(0,\infty)$ functions $t^{(x-1)/2}e^{-t/2}$ and
   149	  $t^{(y-1)/2}e^{-t/2}$ have squared norms $\Gamma_E(x),\Gamma_E(y)$ and inner
   150	  product $\Gamma_E(5/4)$. Cauchy--Schwarz, positivity, inversion and the
   151	  increasing square root prove the bound. At $a = 1/2$, $x = y = 5/4$, giving
   152	  equality. Replacing $a$ by $1-a$ exchanges these two arguments, so only this
   153	  ratio of bound formulas is symmetric, not the moment constant or exponent.
   154	  This proves Corollary~\ref{C:white-relative-width}.
   155	\end{proof}
   156	
   157	This example retains the all-model theorem rather than replacing its scope. The
   158	formal static exponent is $3/2$ as $a\downarrow0$; no interchange of long-time
   159	and temporal-endpoint limits is asserted. Jensen holds for the same canonical
   160	solution, while $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$ remains auxiliary. The read-only Skorohod
   161	comparison at strict spatial Riesz exponent below one does not cover this
   162	spatial-white endpoint. A separate white-time problem cannot be substituted for
   163	$0 < a < 1$. No new Skorohod result, source correction or certified decimal
   164	enclosure is claimed.

     1	import StratonovichHAMAudit.HermiteWord

     3	namespace StratonovichHAMAudit.HermiteWordConsumer
     4	open StratonovichHAMAudit.HermiteWord
     5	
     6	-- Coefficients in the unnormalized probabilists' Hermite basis:
     7	-- x He_n = He_(n+1) + n He_(n-1). This defines the finite recurrence;
     8	-- no assertion about Gaussian L² or polynomial realization is imported.
     9	private def vacuum (n : Nat) : Nat := if n = 0 then 1 else 0
    10	private def insert (_ : Unit) (p : Nat → Nat) (n : Nat) : Nat :=
    11	  (if n = 0 then 0 else p (n-1)) + (n+1) * p (n+1)
    12	private def frame (_ : Unit) (p : Nat → Nat) := p
    13	private def project (N : Nat) (p : Nat → Nat) (n : Nat) :=
    14	  if n ≤ N then p n else 0
    15	private def Good (d : Unit → Nat) (p : Nat → Nat) : Prop :=
    16	  ∀ n, d () < n → p n = 0
    17	
    18	private theorem vacuum_good : Good (fun _ => 0) vacuum := by
    19	  intro n hn
    20	  simp only [vacuum]
    21	  split <;> omega
    22	
    23	private theorem insert_good (d : Unit → Nat) (i : Unit) (p : Nat → Nat)
    24	    (hp : Good d p) : Good (bump i d) (insert i p) := by
    25	  intro n hn
    26	  have hi : i = () := by cases i; rfl
    27	  subst i
    28	  simp [bump] at hn
    29	  have h₁ : p (n-1) = 0 := hp _ (by omega)
    30	  have h₂ : p (n+1) = 0 := hp _ (by omega)
    31	  simp [insert, h₁, h₂]
    32	
    33	private theorem frame_good (d : Unit → Nat) (b : Unit) (p : Nat → Nat)
    34	    (hp : Good d p) : Good d (frame b p) := hp
    35	
    36	private theorem project_fixes (N : Nat) (d : Unit → Nat) (p : Nat → Nat)
    37	    (hd : ∀ c, d c ≤ N) (hp : Good d p) : project N p = p := by
    38	  funext n
    39	  simp only [project]
    40	  split
    41	  · rfl
    42	  · exact (hp n (by have h := hd (); omega)).symm
    43	
    44	private theorem count_length (w : List (Unit × Unit)) : counts w () = w.length := by
    45	  induction w with
    46	  | nil => rfl
    47	  | cons a w ih =>
    48	    have ha : a.1 = () := by cases a with | mk i b => cases i; rfl
    49	    simp [counts, bump, ha, ih]
    50	
    51	-- Actual recurrence consumer, arbitrary word length and cutoff; not a third
    52	-- public claim and not the analytic Hermite/Hilbert realization theorem.
    53	example (w : List (Unit × Unit)) (N : Nat) (hN : w.length ≤ N) :
    54	    cut (project N) insert frame vacuum w = raw insert frame vacuum w := by
    55	  apply cut_eq_raw Good insert frame (project N) vacuum (fun _ => N)
    56	    vacuum_good insert_good frame_good (project_fixes N) w
    57	  intro c
    58	  cases c
    59	  simpa only [count_length] using hN
    60	
    61	-- Four insertions preserve the vacuum self-contraction 3 at cutoff 4.
    62	example : cut (project 4) insert frame vacuum [ ((),()), ((),()), ((),()), ((),()) ] 0 = 3 := by
    63	  decide
    64	-- An insufficient cutoff actually changes the second-order vector.
    65	example : cut (project 1) insert frame vacuum [ ((),()), ((),()) ] 2 = 0 := by decide
    66	example : raw insert frame vacuum [ ((),()), ((),()) ] 2 = 1 := by decide
    67	-- Removing lowering loses the self-contraction, so creation-only is false.
    68	example : raw insert frame vacuum [ ((),()), ((),()) ] 0 = 1 := by decide

    70	end StratonovichHAMAudit.HermiteWordConsumer

  5255	\begin{lemma}[Exact cutoffs for finite Gaussian words]\label{L:finite-word-cutoff}
  5256	  Let $g_{ij}$, $1 \le i \le M$, $1 \le j \le m_i$, be independent standard real
  5257	  Gaussian coordinates, grouped by color $i$, and let $\mathscr{X}$ be a complex
  5258	  Hilbert space. On Gaussian polynomials with coefficients in $\mathscr{X}$ set
  5259	  \[
  5260	    J_i=\sum_{j=1}^{m_i}M_{g_{ij}}\otimes K_{ij},
  5261	  \]
  5262	  where each $K_{ij}$ is bounded on $\mathscr{X}$. Let $F_0,\ldots,F_n$ be
  5263	  bounded operators acting only on $\mathscr{X}$. Fix a word $i_1,\ldots,i_n$,
  5264	  and let $r_i$ be the number of its occurrences of color $i$. If $N_i \ge r_i$
  5265	  and $P$ projects each color onto total Hermite degree at most $N_i$, then, for
  5266	  every $v \in \mathscr{X}$,
  5267	  \begin{equation}\label{E:finite-word-cutoff}
  5268	    \begin{split}
  5269	      &(I\otimes F_n)(PJ_{i_n}P)(I\otimes F_{n-1})\cdots
  5270	      (PJ_{i_1}P)(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v)\\
  5271	      &\qquad=(I\otimes F_n)J_{i_n}(I\otimes F_{n-1})\cdots
  5272	      J_{i_1}(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v).
  5273	    \end{split}
  5274	  \end{equation}
  5275	  The equality holds for finite sums and for Bochner integrals of such words
  5276	  whenever the displayed vector integrals exist.
  5277	\end{lemma}
  5278	
  5279	\begin{proof}
  5280	  In normalized Hermite coordinates, multiplication by $g_{ij}$ maps
  5281	  $h_{\boldsymbol a}$ to $\sqrt{a_{ij}+1}\,h_{\boldsymbol a+e_{ij}}
  5282	  +\sqrt{a_{ij}}\,h_{\boldsymbol a-e_{ij}}$; the second term is zero if $a_{ij}
  5283	  = 0$. Thus, it changes the total degree of color $i$ by one and leaves all
  5284	  other color degrees unchanged. The operators $I\otimes F_l$ leave every
  5285	  Gaussian degree unchanged. After the first $l$ insertions, the uncompressed
  5286	  word therefore has color-$i$ degree at most $r_i(l) = |\{j\le l:i_j=i\}| \le
  5287	  r_i \le N_i$. This is an induction starting from degree zero in every color.
  5288	  Consequently, $P$ is the identity both before and after every insertion along
  5289	  that word. Induction on $l$ now proves \eqref{E:finite-word-cutoff}. The
  5290	  lowering term has been retained: the assertion includes creation followed by
  5291	  annihilation and all resulting self-contractions. Linearity and equality of
  5292	  the vector integrands prove the last assertion. This is an equality of
  5293	  selected finite words, not of full propagators at a fixed cutoff. This proves
  5294	  Lemma~\ref{L:finite-word-cutoff}.
  5295	\end{proof}
